[agent] Progress ledger for the scheduled npm bug-hunt routine (label pm:npm).

Last updated: 2026-10-05T12Z (run 20 with a ledger), main `4646693` (about 30 fixes past `045d7ec`, including #356, #732, #325, #665, #687, #557/#817 and #601/#603), latest release v4.0.0 (previous v3.3.0, both from npm `@socketsecurity/socket-patch`). v5 makes hosted the default, removes `setup`, and makes hosted `rollback` re-resolve upstream registry entries. Cells marked (v4) were last verified on `f6b7fb9`.

## Coverage matrix

Cells are "pass", "fail #N" or "untested". Every cell uses a real npm install. Hosted cells use a local mock of the patch API with `--patch-server-url` pointed at it. Agent and vendored cells use the same mock or a hand-staged `.socket/`. "Cycle" means scan → fresh `npm ci` → `vex` → `rollback` byte-exact. "Suites" means `e2e_redirect_npm_build` + `e2e_vendor_npm_build` with `SOCKET_PATCH_NPM_E2E_REQUIRED=1`.

## npm config that rewrites hosted pins (#812)

`replace-registry-host=always` (npm ≥ 8) rewrites the hosted pin's origin to the configured registry, so `npm ci` / `npm install` fail E404. The hosted scan exits 0 with no warning. **fail #812** on Linux npm 8.19.4 / 10.9.4 / 12.2.0 (project `.npmrc`, env, and user `.npmrc` via `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`). A warm npm cache masks it; test with `npm ci --cache <fresh>`. A hostname value that isn't the hosted origin passes. Vendored isn't affected; npm 6 / 7 don't have the setting.

Other 2026-10-05 passes (Linux): prerelease version (`ms@3.0.0-canary.1`) hosted / vendored / agent cycles (npm 10.9.4); #798 follow-up (npm 12 `npm install` regenerates the twin → `vex` refuses → re-scan wires both → patched); a real `file:` link cycle crawl (npm 10.9.4).

## Agent writes through links (#626)

Agent mode follows a `node_modules` link into a workspace member, a `file:` dir or an `npm link` target, overwrites first-party source, and rollback restores upstream bytes. **fail #626** on Linux npm 6 (`file:`) / 8 / 10 / 12, macOS npm 10.9.7, and Windows npm 8 / 10 / 12, also on v4.0.0. Vendored refuses (`vendor_workspace_member`) and hosted skips with a warning: both pass.

## Alias under `install-strategy=linked` (#852)

npm 9–11 store an alias as `node_modules/.store/lp@<v>-<h>/node_modules/lp`. Agent mode misses that copy. With a plain copy also installed, apply exits 0 and VEX attests `not_affected` while `require('lp')` is unpatched. **fail #852** on Linux npm 9.9.4 / 10.9.4 / 11.6.2. npm 12.2.0 passes (it dedupes into the real-name entry), and hoisted passes (#356 fixed by #738, 2026-10-05T12Z).

## Vendored artifact under `.gitignore` (#831, yarn-classic's issue)

`*.tgz`, `vendor/` and `.socket/` drop the tarball from the commit silently, and a fresh `npm ci` fails ENOENT. With `.socket/` ignored, `vendor --check` exits 0. **fail #831** on Linux npm 8.19.4 / 10.9.4 / 12.2.0 (matrix on #831; draft fix #837).

## Known non-bugs

- Scratch harness tip: a test file that includes `npm_e2e_common` must also include `vex_e2e_common`. `scan` refuses `--offline` (strict airgap), so use `apply` for offline agent cells.

- Mocks of the public proxy need `SOCKET_PROXY_URL` (and `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1`); `--api-url` alone still reaches `patches-api.socket.dev`.
- Project `.npmrc` `allow-remote=${VAR}` is read raw and treated as an explicit user value (warns, doesn't write). Fails safe.
- `patches-api.socket.dev` is unreachable from the sandbox. Use hand-staged manifests, a local mock API, or the wiremock suites.
- Running `scan --mode hosted` from a workspace member directory finds no packages, because discovery is cwd-scoped. It's loud and writes nothing.
- An explicit `allow-remote` other than `all` is respected with a loud `redirect_npm_allow_remote` warning, and a fresh npm 12 install then fails EALLOWREMOTE (fails closed). This is documented.
- `npm update` re-resolves a hosted or vendored entry back to the registry. That's npm's behaviour; `vex` then refuses (`redirect_unwired` / `vendor_unwired`).
- After that, `apply` skips the package as "managed by `socket-patch vendor`" with exit 0 and doesn't take ownership back. That's by design (`apply.rs` `VENDOR_OWNED_MARKER`), and `vex` refuses.
- npm 12 doesn't install the dependencies of a `file:` directory dependency into the linked directory.
- The walk skips `build`, `dist`, `vendor`, `tmp`, `temp`, `coverage` and hidden directories, even when one is an npm workspace member (documented in docs/ecosystems.md).
- `apply` from a workspace member directory reports `noManifest` when `.socket/` lives at the root (`--cwd` scoping).
- Concurrent lock-taking commands fail fast with `lock_held` unless `--lock-timeout` is set (documented).
- `rollback` drops the rolled-back manifest entries and GCs their blobs unless `--preserve-state` is set (documented).
- Agent-mode `vex` omits patches (`ecosystem_not_setup`) when there's no `setup` hook and no `setup.manual` (documented).
- The VEX product `@id` is the raw origin URL for a non-GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket remote (documented in `vex --help`).
- npm ≥ 11 redacts UUID-shaped path segments in `npm root -g` stdout, so `apply -g` misses a global prefix whose path contains a UUID. That's npm's behaviour, it's loud (exit 1), and `--global-prefix` works around it. Not filed.
- The Windows + npm 6 suite cell needs `SOCKET_PATCH_NPM_E2E_LOCK_WRITER_BIN` (an npm ≥ 7 to write the v2 lock). That's a harness requirement.
- On Windows, npm/node can't run in a cwd longer than the Win32 limit, so deep-path cells there can't run.
- Hosted pins on any host other than `patch.socket.dev` or the `--patch-server-url` origin are invisible to `rollback`, `vex`, `list` and `remove` (documented). Mock runs must pass `--patch-server-url`.
- In the sandbox, hosted `rollback` can't reach registry.npmjs.org (the Rust client doesn't trust the proxy CA). Use `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` pointed at a local passthrough.
- npm 6 installs the patched bytes from a hosted lockfileVersion 1 lock (measured on Linux, Node 22). npm-compatibility.md says it fails closed with EINTEGRITY; that's better than documented, not a bug.
- `rollback` re-adds `resolved` under `omit-lockfile-registry-resolved=true`: hosted keeps no ledger, and npm drops the field on its next install.
- A failed hosted lock write (an immutable lock) leaves `allow-remote=all` in `.npmrc`: exit 1, the documented mid-flush I/O residual.
- A bare hosted `scan` wires only the cwd project's lock. A nested non-workspace project warns `redirect_npm_entry_not_found`. `scan . sub` wires both, but `rollback` / `vex` from the root don't see `sub`'s pins (use `--cwd sub`).
- `rollback <path>` path targets select installed copies, so a workspace member whose dependency is hoisted to the root matches nothing (documented).
- Vendored `vex` attests from the committed artifact and only warns `vendored_tree_out_of_sync` when the live tree is stale (documented).
- `scan -g` without `-e` also scans the cargo, pypi and gem global stores (by design). `vex -g` outside a project needs `--product`.
- v5 removes `setup`, so the setup-hook cells are retired.
- Hosted `rollback` restores `resolved` to `registry.npmjs.org` (or `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY`) even when the project `.npmrc` uses a `registry=` mirror. That's documented ("default upstream registry entry"), and `npm ci` still works because of npm's `replace-registry-host`.
- `--package` and `ignorePackages` match package names and purls, not npm alias dependency keys (`lp@npm:left-pad` is matched by `left-pad`, not `lp`).
- npm 12 ignores `ALLOW-REMOTE=` and `allow_remote=` keys in `.npmrc`, so socket-patch appending `allow-remote=all` after them is correct.
- `minSeverity` skips patches whose per-package records carry no severity (documented). Mocks must fill `vulnerabilities` in `by-package`.
- `scan -g --mode agent` run inside a project records the global patch in the cwd `.socket/manifest.json`, and `rollback -g` drops it again. The manifest is cwd-scoped; CLI_CONTRACT "Global scope never touches the project's state" only covers hosted pins and the vendor ledger, and says rollback/remove `-g` "drop their manifest records".
- With no override, npm dedupes a root registry spec (`left-pad@1.3.0`) onto a transitive git copy of the same version, so the lock has a single git entry and the `redirect_npm_non_registry_entry_skipped` skip is correct.
- v4.0.0 agent `vex` omits patches with `ecosystem_not_setup` unless `setup.manual` lists the ecosystem (v4 behaviour). Set it when bisecting vex against v4.
- Hosted `vex` attests an omitted devDependency (`npm ci --omit=dev`) from its lock pin: documented ("With nothing installed … attests from that pin").
- A vendored v2 lock re-saved by npm 7/8 (`npm install`) loses `resolved` in the legacy `dependencies` mirror, because npm's serializer never writes it for a `file:` resolution. A cold-cache npm 6 `npm ci` then fails closed with EINTEGRITY. That's npm's behaviour; npm-compatibility.md's npm 6 + vendored v2 claim holds only until such a re-save.
- `vex` with a bundled (`inBundle`) copy refuses to attest (`patched_ref_unattributable`). In hosted mode the final error reads as "no references found" (exit 2) because a rejected reference keeps nothing alive (documented). Only the diagnostic is misleading.
- `scan --mode agent` over hosted pins keeps the pins and warns (`redirectState`; documented).
- (Retired 2026-10-03T12Z: npm vendored `scan --prune` / `vendor --revert` / `remove` keeping an entry whose lock entry vanished after `npm uninstall` is now tracked as a bug in #665.)
- `package-lock=false` in `.npmrc`: hosted pins are ignored by a plain `npm install` (unpatched), but `npm ci` honors the lock and `vex` refuses `not_applied`. Fails closed; the user's config choice.
- A symlinked `.npmrc` isn't written through (hosted warns that `allow-remote` must be set). A symlinked lock is refused `redirect_symlinked_file_unsupported`.
- Probe mock servers need a readiness loop: a scan that starts before the server listens fails with "tcp connect error: deadline has elapsed" (a probe artifact).
- Lockfile-only discovery skips lockfileVersion 1 locks: on an npm 6 checkout without `node_modules`, `scan` finds 0 packages and prints "No packages found. Run your package manager's install first." (exit 0). The code calls this documented (`vendor/lock_inventory/npm.rs:168`), though the user docs don't say it. It's loud, and installing first works. Not filed.
- A hosted-appended `allow-remote=all` line in a pre-existing `.npmrc` survives `rollback` / `remove` with `npm_allow_remote_left` (documented: v5 keeps no provenance).
- v5 vendoring downloads prebuilt artifacts from `POST …/patches/package`. `--vendor-source build` was removed, and `vendor --offline` over a hand-staged `.socket/` refuses `vendor_service_offline_conflict`. Mocks must serve that endpoint, and the batch mock must return only the requested purls.
- `vex --json` without `--output` exits 2 with `json_requires_output` (documented).
- A lock with git merge-conflict markers: hosted warns `not valid JSON; npm redirect skipped` and exits 0 (same exit-0 contract as bun's invalid lock), vendored exits 1. Loud; not filed.
- `scan --sync` GC deletes a recorded patch's before-blob (`.socket/blobs/<beforeHash>`). That's by design: rollback downloads the before-blob on demand.
- Python mock blob routes must serve the before bytes for the before-hash, or agent `rollback` fails "Content hash mismatch" (a mock artifact).
- npm 12 needs Node ^22.22.2 / ^24.15 / ≥26; the sandbox's Node 22.22.0 is too old. Install `node@24` from npm into a scratch prefix.
- `rollback` / `remove` delete a user-authored project `.npmrc` that is exactly `allow-remote=all\n`, even when it existed before the hosted scan. That's documented (CLI_CONTRACT: a file that is exactly hosted mode's own is deleted, because v5 keeps no provenance).
- npm 12.2.0 installs a copy nested under a `hasShrinkwrap` dependency from the root lock, so hosted / vendored rewrites of it work there. #753 covers npm 6–11 only.
- A dual lock whose shrinkwrap lacks the package and whose package-lock twin has it: lockfile-only discovery reads the shrinkwrap, so `scan` finds nothing and writes nothing (loud; no claim made).
- The sandbox sets `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG=/root/.npmrc`, so a scratch `$HOME/.npmrc` is ignored unless you repoint that variable (a harness artifact).
- `vex -o` is `--org`; the output flag is `-O` / `--output`.
- `vendor --check` verifying only the artifact (not the lock wiring) for npm is tracked in #725 (generic root cause, draft fix #730). Don't re-file it per npm shape.

This is the first run with a ledger. An earlier run on the same day filed #324, #325 and #326 but wrote no entry.

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9` (CLI 4.0.0). Latest release 4.0.0 and previous release 3.3.0, both from npm `@socketsecurity/socket-patch`. npm 6.14.18, 8.19.4, 10.9.7, 11.20.0 (installed, not yet exercised) and 12.1.0 on Node 22.22 (Linux). The probe added npm 10.9.4 and 12.1.0 on ubuntu, macOS and Windows.

**Setup:** the Socket patch API isn't reachable from the sandbox. Agent and vendored cells hand-stage `.socket/manifest.json` plus blobs (a marker prepended to `index.js`). Hosted cells use a ~60-line Python mock of the patch API: batch, by-package, the `patches/package` grant, `patches/view` and the tarball route, with the tarball gzipped with mtime 0 so the sha512 pin is stable across mock restarts. Every hosted cell ends with a fresh-checkout `npm ci` plus `vex`.

## Re-triage

#324, #325 and #326 are still open, their fix PRs (#337 and #345) aren't merged yet, and main is the same commit they were filed on. I didn't re-run them.

## Cells

- **Agent, npm alias** (`"lp": "npm:left-pad@1.3.0"`): **fail → #356** on npm 6, 8, 10 and 12, and on Linux, macOS and Windows. An alias-only project gets `package_not_installed`. A mixed project (plain + alias) patches only the plain copy, and `apply --vex` and `vex` attest `not_affected`. The same happens on 4.0.0 and 3.3.0. Vendored mode rewires the alias entry correctly.
- **Agent, `install-strategy=linked`** (`node_modules/.store`): **fail → #359** on npm 10 and 12, Linux, macOS and Windows. Transitive packages count as lockfile-only. `apply` exits 1, and `scan --apply` exits 0 with `success` while leaving them unpatched. `vendor` gets `package_not_installed`. Direct deps (symlinks) pass. It's the same on 4.0.0 and 3.3.0.
- **Agent, workspaces** (nested conflicting copies in two members): pass. **Agent, bundled copies:** pass (both copies patched).
- **Vendored, workspace nested lock entry** on npm 10 and 12: pass. Fresh `npm ci`, `npm install`, and `npm install <other> -w a` all keep the vendored entry.
- **Hosted, npm 12:** pass for a workspace member's nested entry with a fresh `npm ci` + `vex`; `.npmrc` auto-config with user-config `all` and env `all`; respected env `root` / user-config `none`, which warn loudly and fail closed with EALLOWREMOTE; `npm install` and `npm install <pkg>` keep the redirect on npm 10 and 12; after `npm update` unwires it, `vex` reports `redirect_unwired` and `rollback` removes the `.npmrc` cleanly.
- **setup:** pass. The postinstall + `dependencies` hooks re-patch nested workspace copies on `npm ci` (npm 10 and 12, via `npx` 4.0.0). A CRLF, tab-indented `package.json` with existing scripts round-trips byte-exact through `setup` / `setup --remove`. `apply --silent` on main prints nothing.

## Issues

- Filed #356: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/356 (npm aliases are never patched in agent mode, and VEX attests anyway)
- Filed #359: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/359 (`install-strategy=linked` `.store` copies are invisible, and `scan --apply` exits 0)
- Commented on both with the cross-OS probe results.

## False positives ruled out

- Hosted `scan` from a workspace member directory finds nothing: discovery is cwd-scoped, it's loud and writes nothing.
- An explicit non-`all` `allow-remote` is respected with a warning, and the install fails closed (documented).
- `npm update` dropping a hosted redirect is npm's own behaviour, and `vex` catches it.
- npm 12 doesn't install the dependencies of `file:` directory deps, so there's no copy to patch.
- An early hosted EINTEGRITY came from my mock: gzip mtime changed the tarball between restarts.
- 4.0.0's `apply --silent` token notice doesn't appear on main.

## Probe runs

- https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36758644937 (alias + linked, 3 OS × npm 10.9.4 / 12.1.0). Its jobs are red only because the script's `bash -e` stopped at the expected failing `apply`.
- Deleting `bughunt/npm/20260930-alias-linked` failed (`git push --delete`: "remote end hung up"), so a maintainer needs to delete it.

## Next

1. Windows and macOS for vendored and hosted (autocrlf checkouts, long paths, drive-letter `file:` specs), using the mock API inside a probe.
2. Dual-lock (shrinkwrap + package-lock) drift after `npm install <pkg>` on npm 11 vs 12, and `patched_ref_unattributable`.
3. npm 9.x and 11.20.0 cells; Node 18 and 24 with npm 12.
4. `overrides` to an aliased spec in hosted and vendored modes (related to #356).
5. Concurrent `apply` runs, and an interrupted hosted run (`.npmrc` written, lock unchanged).

## False positives ruled out

- `rollback` removing the manifest entries and GCing their blobs is documented (README command table).
- Agent-mode `vex` exits 1 with `ecosystem_not_setup` when there's no `setup` hook or `setup.manual`. That's documented.
- The VEX product `@id` is the raw origin URL for a non-GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket remote, which is documented (`vex --help`).

2. `npm ci --omit=optional` / `--omit=dev` against a manifest that patches an omitted package (likely the same root cause as #403; check vendored and hosted too).

4. npm `install-links=true` file: directory deps (packed copies) in agent and vendored modes.
5. Interrupted hosted run (`.npmrc` written, lock unchanged), using the wiremock harness.

[agent] 2026-10-01: maintainer note: test global (`-g`) mode for hosted patches

This is a maintainer request, not a run report. Add it to the top of the backlog and keep it there until the cells below are covered.

**Ask:** make sure we correctly scan global installs when `-g` / `--global` is passed, on every major npm version and on Linux, macOS and Windows.

**Where npm puts global installs:** `npm install -g`; discovery via `npm root -g`. Cover the default prefix, a user prefix (`npm config set prefix`), nvm / volta / fnm / Homebrew node, and Windows `%APPDATA%\npm`. Known: npm ≥ 11 redacts UUID path segments in `npm root -g`, so `--global-prefix` is needed there.

**What to check** (prove each with a real global install, not by reading source):
1. `socket-patch scan -g` (no `--mode`) is report-only. It must find every globally installed npm package that has a hosted patch: none missing, no project packages leaking in, correct versions. Also check `--json`.
2. `scan -g` run from inside a npm project versus outside one: `-g` must scan only the global location, and a scan without `-g` must never touch it.
3. `scan -g --mode hosted` and `scan --global-prefix <dir> --mode hosted` must refuse loudly, as designed ("global installs have no project lockfile to redirect"). They must exit non-zero and write nothing.
4. `get -g` defaults to agent mode. Check `scan -g --apply`, `apply -g`, `rollback -g` and `vex -g`: the globally installed copy is actually patched (run the installed tool or import it), rollback restores it byte for byte, and `vex` only attests what's applied.
5. `--global-prefix <dir>` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behave the same as `-g`. That covers custom prefixes, version managers, paths with spaces or unicode, and a non-root user's prefix.
6. A global directory you can't write to (root-owned prefix, Windows Program Files) must fail loudly with a clear error, never exit 0 unpatched.

Add OS × npm version cells for `-g` (scan report / apply / rollback) to the coverage matrix, and use probe branches for macOS and Windows.

Sandbox-only workaround: the Rust client doesn't trust the egress proxy CA, so hosted rollback's registry lookups go through a mock passthrough (`SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:8765/reg`). The CI probes used the real registry.

- #356 (agent mode, npm alias): **still reproduces** on v5. `apply` returns `package_not_installed`. Hosted and vendored handle the alias. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/356#issuecomment-5925920002
- #403 (platform-skipped optional dependency): **still reproduces** (`apply` exits 1). `setup` is gone, but v5 docs tell agent projects to run `apply` in CI. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/403#issuecomment-5925920627

## Cells

- **Hosted full cycle (scan → fresh `npm ci` → `vex` → `rollback` byte-exact):** pass on Linux for: plain packages on npm 10; aliases on npm 10 and on npm 8 (v2 lock, packages half only, see #432); scoped packages on npm 11; nested copies on npm 8 and 10; duplicate nested copies in workspace members on npm 11; a workspace with an alias and a nested member entry on npm 12; dual-lock on npm 12; lockfileVersion 1 on npm 6 (npm 6 **does** install the patched bytes from a hosted v1 lock here, contrary to the "fails closed EINTEGRITY" row in npm-compatibility.md; that's better than documented, so not filed). Probe: it passes on all 6 OS × npm cells (aliases + nested, under a space + unicode path), and `.npmrc` is deleted on rollback.
- **Hosted re-run idempotency:** pass (rollout `already: 3`, lock unchanged). **Lockfile-only checkout and stale tree:** pass (uses the lock version). `--dry-run` writes nothing.
- **Hosted → vendored takeover, then full rollback:** pass on npm 12 with workspaces (git diff empty).
- **Dual-lock drift after `npm install <pkg>`** on npm 11 and 12: pass (`rollback` restores both locks).
- **Path-scoped rollback, `remove <uuid>`, `list`:** pass. `remove --preserve-state` is missing its documented note: **fail → #433**.
- **`omit-lockfile-registry-resolved=true`:** cycle passes, but rollback adds `resolved` back (see known non-bugs).
- **Nested independent project** (`tools/sub`, not a workspace): a bare scan warns `redirect_npm_entry_not_found` and wires only the root. `scan . tools/sub` wires both. Root `rollback` / `vex` don't see `tools/sub`; `--cwd tools/sub` does. Per-project model, loud; not filed.
- **Vendored:** `repair` re-downloads a deleted or tampered artifact (pass). `vendored_tree_out_of_sync` warns only (documented).
- **npm alias in a lockfileVersion 2 legacy mirror:** **fail → #432**. Hosted (silently) and vendored (with a warning) leave `dependencies.<alias>` on the registry, so npm 6 installs unpatched bytes while lockfile-only `vex` returns `not_affected`. 4.0.0 behaves the same. A v1 alias lock in hosted mode writes nothing (`redirect_npm_entry_not_found`, exit 0).
- **Global mode (maintainer checklist):** Linux sandbox npm 10/12, ubuntu and macOS probes: pass for `scan -g` report-only (only global packages, no project leak, no writes; `-g` without `-e` also scans cargo/pypi/gem global stores by design), `--global-prefix` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` parity, `scan -g --mode hosted` refusing with exit 2, `get -g` / `scan -g --mode agent` patching the real global copy, `vex -g --product` attesting only applied patches (it refuses after a reinstall), and `rollback -g` byte-exact. **Windows: fail → #434** (bare `npm` spawn; `scan -g` finds nothing and exits 0; `--global-prefix` works). Not covered: unwritable prefix (sandbox runs as root), nvm/volta/fnm.

## Issues

- Filed #432: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/432
- Filed #433: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/433
- Filed #434: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/434
- Commented on #356 and #403 (above).

## False positives ruled out

- Hosted `rollback` / `vex` "Manifest not found" on mock URLs: hosted pins are only recognized on `patch.socket.dev` or the `--patch-server-url` origin (documented). A mock artifact.
- Hosted rollback registry `error sending request`: the sandbox proxy CA. A sandbox artifact.
- `vex -g` needs `--product` outside a project. Reasonable and loud.
- Rollback re-adding `resolved` under `omit-lockfile-registry-resolved=true`: hosted keeps no ledger, so the restore can't know the field was absent, and npm drops it again on the next install. Harmless.
- A failed hosted lock write (immutable `package-lock.json`) leaves `allow-remote=all` in `.npmrc`. Exit 1, and it's the documented mid-flush I/O residual.
- `rollback ./packages/a` matches nothing when a's dependency is hoisted to the root (path targets select installed copies; documented).

## Probe branches

`bughunt/npm/20261001-v5-hosted-global` (runs 36824736862 and 36825128447; the first run's npm 12 cells failed because npm 12 needs Node ≥ 24.15) and `bughunt/npm/20261001-win-global` (run 36826141655). `git push --delete` prints "Everything up-to-date" through the proxy and deletes nothing. **A maintainer needs to delete these two plus the five older ones.**

2. Hosted mode with a custom `.npmrc` `registry=` mirror: does rollback restore to npmjs.org instead of the mirror (documented "default upstream"), and does `npm ci` then work?
3. `npm ci --omit=optional` / `--omit=dev` against hosted and vendored entries plus `vex`.
4. v5 `socket.yml` policy (`minSeverity`, `maxNewPatches`) and `--package` filters on npm workspaces.
5. Node 18 with npm 9/10, and npm 12 on Node 26.

That's documented ("default upstream registry entry", `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY`), and npm's `replace-registry-host` keeps `npm ci` working. `allow-remote=all` stays, with the documented `npm_allow_remote_left` warning.
- **`.npmrc` variants for allow-remote:** no trailing newline, CRLF, BOM, `allow-remote = all` (spaces), quoted `"all"`, `ALLOW-REMOTE=…`, `allow_remote=…`, a trailing `[section]`, and explicit `none`: pass. npm 12 ignores the uppercase and underscore keys (`npm config get` checked), so appending is correct. Spaces and quotes count as already set. The CRLF line ending is preserved. On npm 12, a fresh `npm ci` passes for the mirror, spaces and CRLF variants.
- **`overrides`** (flat, alias `npm:` and nested) × npm 8.19.4 / 10 / 11.20.0, hosted: pass. Fresh `npm ci` gets the patched bytes, and a later `npm install` keeps the pin.

- `socket_yml_invalid`: my socket.yml had no `version: 2`. Documented.

4. Re-verify #326 (git deps) and #359 (linked transitive, agent mode) on v5.

[agent] 2026-10-01: handover from the Deno bug-hunt routine (ledger #308): agent-mode `vex` attests not_affected while other nested copies of the same name@version are unpatched

Found while testing Deno's hoisted linker. The root cause is generic npm-family, and the realistic trigger is plain npm, so this is yours to file. Nothing was filed from Deno. I searched for duplicates (#325, #405, #435, #471 are bundled / hosted / isolated / global variants) and found none covering agent mode.

**Defect.** In agent mode `vex` hashes only the **first** installed copy of each PURL: `crates/socket-patch-cli/src/commands/vex.rs:556` `let package_paths = collapse_to_first(copies.clone());`. Every other copy is ignored, while hosted-basis PURLs check every copy (`vex_consumed`). CLI_CONTRACT's verification table says agent evidence is "the installed tree". When the first copy is patched and another copy of the same `name@version` isn't, vex emits `not_affected` for a package whose unpatched copy is still loaded at runtime. The verdict depends on crawl order: revert the first copy instead and vex correctly says `not_applied`.

**Realistic trigger (real npm 10.9.4, main `61cfb9b`, Linux, reproduced 2/2).** `apply` patches every copy present, then a later `npm install` of new dependents extracts fresh, unpatched nested copies and leaves the old patched one alone:

```sh
mkdir npmdup && cd npmdup && echo '{"name":"npmdup","version":"1.0.0"}' > package.json
npm install kind-of@6.0.3 is-number@3.0.0          # nests kind-of@3.2.2 under is-number
# offline manifest + blobs patching package/index.js of pkg:npm/kind-of@3.2.2 (any free patch works)
socket-patch apply --offline                         # applied 1
npm install is-accessor-descriptor@0.1.6             # adds node_modules/is-accessor-descriptor/node_modules/kind-of@3.2.2 (unpatched)
socket-patch vex --offline -O v.json                 # exit 0, 1 statement: not_affected pkg:npm/kind-of@3.2.2
```

Copies afterwards: `is-number/node_modules/kind-of` patched, `is-accessor-descriptor/node_modules/kind-of` **unpatched**. A re-run of `apply` does patch the new copies (`applied: 2, skipped: 1`), so apply is fine; only vex is wrong.

**Deno too:** `nodeModulesLinker: "hoisted"` (2.9.7) with `kind-of@6.0.3` + `is-number@3.0.0` + `is-accessor-descriptor@0.1.6` gives two nested `kind-of@3.2.2` copies. Reverting the `is-accessor-descriptor` copy → vex `not_affected`. Reverting the `is-number` copy → `not_applied`. Same crawl-order dependence. It's likely the same for yarn classic, bun hoisted and pnpm (multiple `.pnpm` peer variants of one version).

Expected: agent vex attests a PURL only when every installed copy the crawler finds verifies (the hosted path already does this), otherwise it omits it as `not_applied` / `hash_mismatch`.

The branch delete failed through the proxy again ("remote end hung up"), so it joins the stale-branch list.

## Cells (Linux unless noted)

- **Hosted `npm ci --omit=dev` + `vex`** (npm 10): pass. The omitted devDependency is attested from its lock pin, which CLI_CONTRACT documents ("With nothing installed … attests from that pin").
- **Vendored cycle with `--omit=dev`**, nested copy, revert: pass on npm 7.0.15, 7.24.2, 8.19.4, 9.9.4, 10.9.4, 11.21.0, 12.2.0 (Node 24 and 26). On npm 6 with a v1 lock it refuses loudly with `vendor_lockfile_version_unsupported`, which is documented.
- **Hosted cycle** (alias, nested, devDependency, byte-exact rollback): pass on npm 7.0.15, 7.24.2, 9.9.4, and 12.2.0 on Node 26.
- **Workspaces** (a member's nested copy, root + member deps), vendored and hosted: pass on npm 7.0.15, 7.24.2, 8.19.4, 10, 12.
- **`npm-shrinkwrap.json` as the only lock**, hosted: pass on npm 6 (v1) and npm 8 (v2).
- **A `file:` tarball dependency that ships its own `npm-shrinkwrap.json`** (its nested copy pinned by it), hosted, with `npm ci` and `npm install`: pass.
- **Mixed-case legacy name** (`JSONStream`), hosted cycle: pass.
- **npm 12 hosted with `install-strategy=linked`**: pass. Rollback leaves `allow-remote=all` in a mixed `.npmrc` (documented `npm_allow_remote_left`).
- **`allow-remote=all` already set** in the env var or `~/.npmrc` when scanning: the project `.npmrc` is still written, so teammates' npm 12 `npm ci` works. Pass.
- **Takeovers** vendored↔hosted (npm 7.24.2, 8.19.4, 12) and agent↔hosted/vendored (npm 10): pass, byte-exact undo. hosted→agent keeps the pins with a loud warning plus `redirectState` (documented).
- **Rescan idempotency** (vendored and hosted, npm 8 and 12): pass, nothing rewritten.
- **`remove <purl>`** for a member's nested copy in a workspace, hosted and vendored on npm 12: pass.
- **Agent cycle on npm 7.0.15 / 7.24.2:** apply, `vex`, `npm ci` (`vex` then refuses), re-apply and rollback: pass.
- **A bundled (`inBundle`) copy of a vendored or hosted patch:** pass. `vex` refuses to attest (`patched_ref_unattributable`). The hosted variant's final error then says "no hosted or vendored patch references were found … Run `socket-patch scan` first" (exit 2), although the warning just above names the rejected reference. That follows the documented rule that a rejected mention keeps nothing alive. Only the diagnostic is misleading, so I didn't file it.

None filed, commented on or closed. Nothing new met the bar.

[agent] 2026-10-02: handover from the Bun bug-hunt routine (#306). Not filed: the behaviour is in the npm-family agent crawler, not Bun-specific, and could be by design.

**Observation:** in agent mode, `socket.yml` path policy judges only the scan root (`--cwd`). Independent nested projects (each with its own lockfile) under the root are crawled into project `""`, so `patches.ignorePaths` / `includePaths` and the built-in `tests/` default never exclude them.

Repro (main `61cfb9b`, Linux, 2/2 runs; a local mock API; nested projects installed with Bun 1.4.2, plus a root `package-lock.json` via npm 10):
```
repo/ (.git, package.json + package-lock.json: left-pad@1.3.0)
  apps/web/       bun.lock  is-number@6.0.0
  apps/api/       bun.lock  is-odd@3.0.1
  services/legacy bun.lock  left-pad@1.3.0, is-number@6.0.0
  tests/e2e/      bun.lock  is-number@6.0.0
socket.yml: version: 2 / patches: ignorePaths: ["/services/"]
socket-patch scan --mode agent --yes --json   # at repo root
```
- Result: `success`, `policy.counts {filtered: 0, retained: 0}`, and `services/legacy/node_modules/left-pad/index.js` is patched.
- With `includePaths: ["/*", "!/*/"]` (CLI_CONTRACT: "targets only the repo-root project"), every nested project's copy is patched, including `tests/e2e` (a default-ignored dir).
- Code: `ScanPolicy::for_root` (crates/socket-patch-cli/src/commands/scan/policy.rs:141) evaluates `admits_root` once, for the cwd. Agent PATH globs (`scan 'services/**' --mode agent`) also report `filtered: 0`.
- Hosted and vendored modes are fine: `scan '*/*' --mode hosted|vendored` runs per directory, and the policy is honoured there.

Related, also generic and not filed: hosted/vendored PATH globs (`project_dirs`, scan/mod.rs:1314, `glob::glob` with default options) match dot-dirs and `node_modules`. So `scan '*/*'` visits `.git/hooks`, `.git/objects`… (printing "No packages found"), and `scan 'apps/**'` visits `apps/*/node_modules/<pkg>`. It's noise only in my runs; nothing was written there.

Your call whether either one is a bug under CLI_CONTRACT "socket.yml patch policy" → Paths.

[agent] Handover from the vlt bug-hunt routine (ledger #307): npm vendored `scan --prune` doesn't revert an entry whose dependency left package-lock.json

Found while filing #541 (vlt), which uses npm as the control. Main `61cfb9b`, Linux, npm 10 / package-lock v3, local mock registry plus patch API (see #307).

```bash
echo 'registry=http://127.0.0.1:18555/' > .npmrc
echo '{"name":"app","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"left-pad":"1.3.0"}}' > package.json; npm install
socket-patch scan --mode vendored --yes                  # rc 0
echo '{"name":"app","version":"1.0.0","dependencies":{"left-pad":"1.2.0"}}' > package.json; npm install
socket-patch scan --mode vendored --yes                  # rc 1, vendor_lock_entry_not_found
socket-patch scan --mode vendored --prune --yes --json   # rc 1, gc.revertedVendoredEntries = []  <- npm-specific
socket-patch scan --mode vendored --yes                  # rc 1 again: stuck
```

On vlt, the same `--prune` run reverts the entry (`revertedVendoredEntries: ["pkg:npm/left-pad@1.3.0"]`) and the next run is rc 0. That points at npm's `dispatch_in_use_one` (`crates/socket-patch-cli/src/commands/vendor.rs:260`) not answering `Some(false)` for a package-lock that now holds only `node_modules/left-pad@1.2.0`. CLI_CONTRACT.md says leg (b) of `scan --prune` reverts "EVERY ledger entry whose dependency is no longer in the lockfile graph". I haven't filed it; it's yours to verify. The shared part (the rescan / prune exit 1 caused by the ledger supplement) is #541.

[agent] 2026-10-02: handover from the Bun bug-hunt routine (#306). Not filed: the behaviour lives in the shared npm-family VEX discovery and reproduces identically with npm 10, so it isn't Bun-specific. It might also be by design, since CLI_CONTRACT's vendored row attests from "the committed artifact + lock wiring".

**Observation:** a vendored (and, under `--no-verify`, a hosted) `vex` attests `not_affected` for `name@version` when the lockfile wires one copy of it to the Socket artifact and a second, plain **registry** entry of the same `name@version` in the **same** lockfile is left unwired. That second copy installs unpatched. `contest_across_locks` (`vex/discover/mod.rs:574`) and `push_uncontested` (`vex/discover/npm.rs:99`, `*j != i`) only contest refs across *different* locks. #325 / #326 / #497 handle bundled and non-registry copies in the same lock, but not an unwired registry copy.

**A natural way to get there:** run vendored (or hosted) scan, then add a workspace member that depends on the same `name@version` and run `npm install` / `bun install`. The package manager resolves the new nested copy from the registry. Re-running `scan` heals it (verified), but in between `vex` attests.

Repro (main `61cfb9b`, Linux, 2/2 runs each, local mock API; the patch is for `pkg:npm/is-number@6.0.0`):
```sh
# root: is-number@7.0.0, workspaces packages/*; packages/a: is-number@6.0.0
npm install && socket-patch scan --mode vendored --yes        # packages/a/node_modules/is-number → file:.socket/vendor/…
# add packages/b with is-number@6.0.0
npm install                                                    # packages/b/node_modules/is-number → registry 6.0.0 (unpatched bytes)
socket-patch vex --json --product pkg:npm/app@1.0.0 -O vex.json   # verified pkg:npm/is-number@6.0.0 (also with --no-verify)
```
Bun (1.4.2, text v2 workspace lock): the same with `c/is-number: ["is-number@6.0.0", "", {}, …]` beside the rewired entries. Vendored `vex` (default and `--no-verify`) attests. Hosted default `vex` correctly skips it (it hashes the installed copies), but hosted `vex --no-verify` attests. Bun 1.1.45 `bun.lockb`: hosted default skips, which is correct.

**Expected (suggestion):** treat an unwired registry entry of the same `name@version` in the same lock like the #326 non-registry case: no attestation, plus a diag ("re-run scan to rewire every copy").

**What:** after an agent-mode apply is interrupted, or after any reinstall that restores unpatched bytes while `.socket/manifest.json` still records the patches, plain `socket-patch scan --mode agent` (human output) does **not** re-apply. - Code: `crates/socket-patch-cli/src/commands/scan/mod.rs` ~2733–2771 (the human path partitions out `already_recorded` and returns early).

The human message names the remedy, and `vex` stays honest (`not_applied`) throughout, so this may be by design. I'm not filing it; it's handed over in case npm's routine wants to judge the human-vs-JSON divergence against CLI_CONTRACT.

9. Re-verify the open set when fixes land: #362, #435, #466, #492, #556, #590 (PR #598; include member-cwd `list`), #627 (PR #802), #633, #713, #714, #734, #756, #778, #830, #831 (PR #837, pnpm gitignore matrix), #853 and #854.
10. Vendored on Windows and macOS (autocrlf: expect the `vendor_lockfile_crlf_unsupported` refusal, and the #853 un-hosting when switching from hosted; check that hosted handles the same checkout; hosted CRLF passes on Linux).

## Known non-bugs

- `patches-api.socket.dev` and (for the Rust client) `registry.npmjs.org` are unreachable from the sandbox. Mock the API and point `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` at a mirror.
- v5 recognises hosted pins only on the configured patch server. Against a mock without `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL`, `rollback` says "Manifest not found". That's a fixture artifact.
- v5 hosted rollback and takeover keep a user-edited `trustLockfile: true` and warn `pnpm_trust_lockfile_left`. A workspace file that exactly matches hosted mode's scaffold is deleted, including a user's own `packages: ['.']` file that the trust append made identical to it (CLI_CONTRACT, upstream restore). The same applies when the user's pre-existing workspace file held only other keys (for example `lockfileIncludeTarballUrl`): the hosted-added `trustLockfile: true` stays, with the warning (v5 records no provenance).
- pnpm 10 ignores `enableGlobalVirtualStore` when `CI` is set, so the global-virtual-store cells don't engage on GH runners with pnpm 10.
- pnpm 12 (and 11) ignore `.npmrc` for `virtual-store-dir` / `enable-global-virtual-store`. Put them in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, or in the global `config.yaml`.
- pnpm 11+ `pnpm root -g` / `pnpm add -g` fail unless `$PNPM_HOME/bin` is on `PATH`. Put it there in fixtures.
- Vendored refusals that are intended, loud and fail-closed: a CRLF `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`vendor_lockfile_crlf_unsupported`), a BOM package.json (`vendor_pkg_json_unsupported`), an inline / flow `overrides:` mapping (`vendor_override_conflict`, unit-tested), and `patchedDependencies` on the target (`vendor_lock_entry_unsupported`; the detail wrongly says "peer-suffixed snapshot key", which is cosmetic). On a hosted → vendored takeover these refusals fire after the hosted pin is already restored, which is #853.
- Vendored `vex` attests from the committed artifact plus lock wiring even when the tree isn't installed. That's by design (CLI_CONTRACT "Manifest-less VEX").
- `vex -g` needs `--product` outside a project ("Could not auto-detect a top-level product PURL").
- Agent-mode `get <purl>` for an uninstalled package reports `success, applied: 1` when another manifest entry applies. The nested apply fails only when nothing matches. It's not pnpm-specific (noted on #362).
- A compact single-line `package.json` comes back 2-space-indented after vendor + rollback. There's no indent to detect, and indented files round-trip byte-exactly, so it's cosmetic.
- Hosted on pnpm 9 over an existing upstream `node_modules`: a frozen install keeps the upstream bytes. That's documented in the `redirect_pnpm_trust_lockfile` warning, and VEX doesn't attest it.
- pnpm 12 warns that `package.json` `pnpm.overrides` is ignored on vendored projects. The workspace-file override is what takes effect, so this is noise only.
- A `vex --output /dev/stdout` hang when stdout is a pipe is not pnpm-specific.
- Vendored refuses pnpm catalogs (`catalogs:` entry) and peer-suffixed snapshot keys with `vendor_lock_entry_unsupported` ("this lock shape is not supported yet"). It's loud and writes nothing. Hosted handles both. (The takeover from hosted un-hosts first: #853.)
- pnpm 10's `configDependencies` copy (`node_modules/.pnpm-config/`) stays unpatched under hosted mode while VEX attests the regular copy. Config deps run only at install time, and pnpm 10 keeps their integrity in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
- On v5, vendoring always downloads its artifact from the patch service (`--vendor-source build` was removed), so offline vendoring with only a staged manifest fails with `vendor_service_offline_conflict`. Fixtures need the mock grant to match the manifest UUID.
- `rush update --full` re-resolves the Rush lock and drops the hosted pin, like `pnpm update`. VEX then honestly reports nothing to attest.
- pnpm 9.15.9's frozen install fails on its own unmodified lock when a workspace uses `dependenciesMeta.injected` ("importer dependencies meta (undefined) doesn't match"). That's upstream pnpm, not socket-patch.
- Old pnpm needs an old Node (≤ 6 needs Node 16, ≤ 2 needs Node 10), and pnpm 3 takes `--store` rather than `--store-dir`. Fixture notes.
- Agent apply over a pnpm `patchedDependencies` edit to the same file overwrites it with the verified patched content and warns `content_mismatch_overwritten` (documented default mismatch policy; `--strict` refuses). Hosted composes both patches, and `vex` then declines (`no_applicable_patches`), because the file matches neither hash.
- Hosted on pnpm 11/12 respects an explicit `trustLockfile: false` (any YAML spelling) and warns `redirect_pnpm_trust_lockfile` with the remedy. The following frozen install fails, which is documented.
- Vendored refuses pnpm ≤ 6 locks (5.x up to 5.3) with `vendor_lockfile_version_unsupported`, and pnpm 7/8 workspace locks with `vendor_lock_entry_unsupported`. pnpm 7/8 vendored locks carry an absolute `file:` specifier (`vendor_pnpm_legacy_absolute_specifier`), so a moved checkout needs `pnpm install --offline --no-frozen-lockfile` once. Both are documented.
- pnpm 11+ ignores `package.json` `pnpm.patchedDependencies`. Put it in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
- A dead-registry fresh install fails when the fixture has any unpatched dependency (it still needs the registry). Use the live registry for those fixtures, or patch every dependency. The same goes for `--offline` with an empty store (`ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL`).
- Vendored from a workspace member cwd fails closed with `vendor_lockfile_missing` (`partial_failure`). Hosted's silent success in the same layout is #590.
- A `package.json` without a trailing newline gains one after vendor + revert. That's a fixture artifact; files that end in a newline round-trip byte-exactly.
- Bundled-copy fixtures need a registry-served host package. A `file:` tarball host (`.pnpm/bundler@file+…`) is patched correctly, so it doesn't reproduce #601.
- pnpm ≤10 `.npmrc` keys must be kebab-case (`modules-dir`, `virtual-store-dir-max-length`); camelCase is silently ignored. pnpm 7–10.11 keep the virtual store in `node_modules/.pnpm` even with `modules-dir`, so agent mode passes there.
- pnpm `file:` directory dependencies are copied into the store (`.pnpm/<name>@file+…`), so patching that copy is correct and doesn't touch the source (unlike `link:` / `workspace:`, #626).
- In-run `scan --mode hosted --vex` attests from this run's records without hash verification, so it says `not_affected` over an upstream install (CLI_CONTRACT `(redirected)` row). Use standalone `vex` after the install as the oracle.
- A `pnpm patch-commit` over a hosted pin makes `vex` decline with `hash_mismatch` (the file matches neither hash). That's honest. Rollback keeps the user's patch and restores the upstream pin.
- pnpm ≤10 `patch-commit` under `CI=true` runs a frozen install and fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH` (fixture note: use `confirmModulesPurge=false`, not `CI`). A mock `/registry` must serve the real npmjs tarball, or a rollback restores a foreign integrity.
- Rush has no root `package.json`, so `vex` needs `--product` there (`product_undetected`), like `-g`.
- pnpm 12.0.0 doesn't run under Rush 5.180 (it rejects Rush's `--no-prefer-frozen-lockfile`). Rush subspace fixtures need `common/config/subspaces/<name>/` folders created and `common/config/rush/.pnpmfile.cjs` removed before `rush update`.
- pnpm 11.28.3 `pnpm install --no-prefer-frozen-lockfile` re-resolves hosted pins to upstream even with `trustLockfile: true` (9 / 10 / 12 keep them). That's upstream pnpm behaviour; the default `pnpm install` and `--frozen-lockfile` keep the pin. It's tracked inside #713 because Rush uses that flag by default.
- `pnpm dedupe` re-resolves and drops hosted pins on every pnpm version (like `pnpm update`). pnpm 11.0.0 / 11.28.3 `pnpm add <other>` also drops them (9 / 10 / 12 keep them). That's upstream pnpm 11 re-resolution, tracked with #713.
- `repair` in the default diff mode needs `/v0/orgs/<org>/patches/diff/<uuid>` archives. A mock without them gives `download_failed`; use `--download-mode file` with a blob route.
- pnpm 11 / 12 `pnpm fetch` with only `pnpm-lock.yaml` copied (no `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) fails loudly with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_URL_MISMATCH`. Commit and copy the trust config, as documented.
- Hosted standalone `vex` attests an optional dependency that isn't installed on this OS (for example `fsevents` on Linux) from its lock pin. That's the documented manifest-less attestation ("nothing installed → attests from the pin").
- pnpm 11 / 12 fail `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` for `esbuild` even on the first install, unless builds are allowed. That's upstream; the patched bytes still land.
- `pnpm update <pkg>` drops the hosted pins of every package it re-resolves (pnpm 12 also re-resolves the package's dependents), like `pnpm update`.
- Agent `apply` from a pnpm workspace member cwd patches only the member's direct (linked) deps. Transitive deps in the root `.pnpm` are skipped ("No installed package matches this PURL", exit 0), and agent `vex` omits them (`package_not_found`). Agent crawls are cwd-scoped, and CLI_CONTRACT puts a member that shares the root lock in the root project, so run from the root.
- Hosted on a `pnpm-lock.yaml` with git conflict markers writes nothing and warns `redirect_pnpm_entry_not_found` for every package (exit 0). It fails safe. Resolve the conflict (`pnpm install`) first.
- Hosted leaves a `file:` tarball or git dependency that shares a patched name@version alone (`redirect_pnpm_entry_not_found`), and `vex` doesn't attest it.
- pnpm 12 `pnpm deploy` writes its own `pnpm-workspace.yaml` without the hosted `trustLockfile: true`, so a re-install inside the deploy output fails loudly (`ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_URL_MISMATCH`). That's upstream pnpm; ship the deployed `node_modules`, or add `trustLockfile: true` there. pnpm 9 / 10 deploy outputs re-install patched.
- pnpm 10 `pnpm deploy` (shared lockfile) fails with "Deployment with a shared lockfile has failed" for any `file:` tarball override, the user's own included. That's upstream, so vendored + deploy on pnpm 10 is blocked by pnpm itself.
- A deploy of a vendored project gets an absolute `file://…/.socket/vendor/…` specifier, and `vex` in the deploy dir declines (no ledger there). The bytes are patched; nothing is falsely attested.
- `pnpm install --resolution-only` on pnpm 9 / 10 re-resolves and drops hosted pins, like `pnpm update` (pnpm 12 keeps them). `prune`, `install --prod` and a plain `install` keep the pin on 9 / 10 / 12.
- Agent `scan --sync <scope>` / `--prune <scope>` where the scope matches nothing (#778) skips the prune with a warning and keeps the manifest. It fails safe.
- Hosted `vex` recognises a hosted pin only when the tarball URL is on the patch-server origin AND carries the patch uuid as a path segment. Mock fixtures need `/…/<uuid>/<file>.tgz` URLs.
- Agent → hosted takeover keeps the agent-mode manifest beside the new hosted pin (`list` shows each patch twice). The layers coexist, and `rollback` unwinds both. Agent → vendored migrates the manifest record out, as documented.
- Vendored `list` keeps listing a package after `pnpm remove <pkg>`, because pnpm keeps the override and the wiring is still live. `vex` omits it.
- Fixture note: `scan -g` also covers the npm global root, so it patches npm's own bundled deps (for example `/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/npm/node_modules/jsonparse`). That isn't pnpm-specific, but it can make a pnpm-global copy look `already_patched` in `apply -g` output.
- Vendored refuses a user parent-selector (`a>b`) or range-selector (`b@<2`) override for the target with `vendor_override_conflict` and writes nothing. The detail text is slightly off (it mentions an exact-pin takeover, or "package.json" on pnpm 12), which is cosmetic. (A bare-key exact pin in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is NOT a genuine conflict: #854.)
- An API that answers with lowercased npm purls for a mixed-case installed name (`Base64`) isn't matched by agent apply (`package_not_installed`). There's no evidence the real API lowercases, so treat it as hypothetical (run 20).
- `scan --mode vendored --dry-run` over a hosted pin previews only `would_vendor` (no `vendor_would_revert_redirect`). It's not pnpm-specific, so it isn't filed here (run 21).

[agent] 2026-09-30: pnpm bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9` (CLI 4.0.0 workspace version), latest release 4.0.0 (previous 3.3.0, both installed from npm for comparison). pnpm 7.33.7, 8.15.9, 9.15.9, 10.0.0, 10.5.2, 10.12.1, 10.34.5, 11.27.0, 12.4.2 and 12.8.1 (the current `latest`), on Node 22 in the sandbox. Patch data is a hand-staged `.socket/manifest.json` plus blobs (agent and vendored mode) and a local Python mock of the patch API and tarball routes (hosted mode). No secrets.

This is the first run: no earlier ledger, and no open `pm:pnpm` issues to re-triage.

### Cells
- **fail #361**: agent `apply` / `rollback` with `enableGlobalVirtualStore`. Writes land in the shared `<store>/links` dir: an unrelated project is patched, and one project's rollback unpatches another. Fails on Linux with pnpm 10.12.1–12.8.1, and on the macOS and Windows probe with pnpm 11.27.0 and 12.8.1. Releases 3.3.0 and 4.0.0 behave the same.
- **fail #362**: agent `apply` on a transitive dep with a custom `virtualStoreDir` (pnpm 8–12) or the global virtual store (10.12+) is reported `package_not_installed`. Fails on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- **fail #360**: vendored mode on pnpm 10.5.2, 10.12.1 and 10.34.5 with user `overrides:` in pnpm-workspace.yaml. `vendor` succeeds, then a fresh `--frozen-lockfile` install fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH`, and a re-lock drops the user's overrides. Passes on 10.0.0, 11.27.0 and 12.8.1. Release 4.0.0 has the same bug.
- pass: vendored lifecycle on pnpm 10.34.5 and 11.27.0 (vendor → fresh frozen `--offline` install → vex → revert). Also passes with `nodeLinker: hoisted` and with a flow `packages: ['.']` plus `catalog: {…}`.
- pass: agent `apply` / `rollback` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` (pnpm 11.27.0). The CAS file is not written through.
- pass: hosted `scan --mode hosted` on pnpm 11.27.0 against the mock API: fresh frozen install with an empty store gets the patched bytes. trustLockfile handling passes for CRLF, no-EOL and trailing-comment `trustLockfile: true` workspace files.
- fail, not filed (queued in the backlog): hosted trustLockfile append and vendored overrides append on a *whole-document flow* `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`{packages: [.]}`) or a file ending in `...`. The command reports success, then pnpm can't parse the file ("end of the stream or a document separator is expected"). Reproduced on pnpm 11.27.0.
- refused, as designed: vendored with a CRLF `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` (`vendor_lockfile_crlf_unsupported`), a BOM package.json (`vendor_pkg_json_unsupported`), inline `overrides: {}` / `{x: y}` (`vendor_override_conflict`, covered by the `inline_workspace_overrides_mapping_is_refused` unit test), and `patchedDependencies` on the target (`vendor_lock_entry_unsupported`).

### Issues
- Filed #360, #361 and #362.

### False positives ruled out
- Vendored `vex` attesting `not_affected` in a fresh clone whose install failed is by design: vendored VEX stands on the committed artifact plus lock wiring (CLI_CONTRACT "Manifest-less VEX"; `vendored_tree_out_of_sync` is a warning only).
- The global virtual store "not reproducing" with pnpm 10.34.5 on GH runners is expected: pnpm 10 disables it when `CI` is set. pnpm 11+ keeps it.
- `vex --output /dev/stdout` hangs when stdout is a pipe. It's not pnpm-specific, so it wasn't filed here; it's noted for whoever owns the CLI.

### Probe
- `bughunt/pnpm/20260930-virtual-store`, run https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36759597534 (ubuntu, macos and windows × pnpm 10.34.5, 11.27.0 and 12.8.1). **The branch could not be deleted:** the git proxy dropped `git push --delete` three times ("unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet"). A maintainer needs to delete it.

### Next
1. Flow-style or `...`-terminated `pnpm-workspace.yaml` breaking under the hosted trust append and the vendored overrides append. Confirm on pnpm 10 and 12, then file.
2. Hosted mode on pnpm 7/8 (lock 5.4/6.0) workspaces with catalogs, and peer-suffixed instances with the mock API. Then Rush/subspace locks.
3. The vendored takeover (hosted → vendored → hosted) on pnpm 11/12, plus `rollback` byte-exactness of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
4. Agent `apply` with `injected` workspace deps (`dependenciesMeta.injected`) and `package-import-method=clone/copy`.
5. pnpm 1–6 legacy layouts (`node_modules/.registry.npmjs.org`, pnpm 4/5 nested host dirs) on Node 16 for agent mode.

[agent] 2026-10-01: maintainer note: test global (`-g`) mode for hosted patches

This is a maintainer request, not a run report. Add it to the top of the backlog and keep it there until the cells below are covered.

**Ask:** make sure we correctly scan global installs when `-g` / `--global` is passed, on every major pnpm version and on Linux, macOS and Windows.

**Where pnpm puts global installs:** `pnpm add -g`; discovery via `pnpm root -g` (`PNPM_HOME`). Cover pnpm 7–10 global-dir layouts, the global virtual store, and pnpm installed through corepack, standalone and npm.

**What to check** (prove each with a real global install, not by reading source):
1. `socket-patch scan -g` (no `--mode`) is report-only. It must find every globally installed pnpm package that has a hosted patch: none missing, no project packages leaking in, correct versions. Also check `--json`.
2. `scan -g` run from inside a pnpm project versus outside one: `-g` must scan only the global location, and a scan without `-g` must never touch it.
3. `scan -g --mode hosted` and `scan --global-prefix <dir> --mode hosted` must refuse loudly, as designed ("global installs have no project lockfile to redirect"). They must exit non-zero and write nothing.
4. `get -g` defaults to agent mode. Check `scan -g --apply`, `apply -g`, `rollback -g` and `vex -g`: the globally installed copy is actually patched (run the installed tool or import it), rollback restores it byte for byte, and `vex` only attests what's applied.
5. `--global-prefix <dir>` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behave the same as `-g`. That covers custom prefixes, version managers, paths with spaces or unicode, and a non-root user's prefix.
6. A global directory you can't write to (root-owned prefix, Windows Program Files) must fail loudly with a clear error, never exit 0 unpatched.

Add OS × pnpm version cells for `-g` (scan report / apply / rollback) to the coverage matrix, and use probe branches for macOS and Windows.

[agent] 2026-10-01: pnpm bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `2463257` (#277, the v5 consolidation; the CLI still reports 4.0.0), latest release 4.0.0 (npm `@socketsecurity/socket-patch@4.0.0`) for regression checks, and draft PR #365's head `80f4a71` for the global cells. pnpm 7.33.7, 8.15.9, 9.15.9, 10.34.5, 11.0.0, 11.27.0, 11.28.3, 12.4.2, 12.8.1 and 12.8.2, on Node 22 in the Linux sandbox. The patch API is a local Python mock (batch, by-package, view with inline blobs, package grant, hosted tarball, plus a `/registry/<name>/<ver>` mirror). This run focused on the maintainer's global (`-g`) request.

**v5 harness note:** hosted pins are recognised only on the named patch server, so set `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL=<mock>`. Rollback restores upstream from the registry, and the Rust client can't reach registry.npmjs.org from the sandbox, so set `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY=<mock>/registry`. Without these, `rollback` reports "Manifest not found" or `cannot restore … upstream registry entry`. Both are fixture artifacts.

### Re-triage
- #401: **closed as fixed by #277.** v5 keeps no redirect ledger. The hosted → vendored takeover (`vendor` and `scan --mode vendored`) on pnpm 11.27.0 and 12.8.1 now emits the documented `pnpm_trust_lockfile_left` advisory, and a workspace file that exactly matches the scaffold is deleted. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/401#issuecomment-5926488624
- #360: still reproduces on `2463257` (pnpm 10.34.5, 2/2, through `scan --mode vendored`). Comment: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/360#issuecomment-5926489471
- #400 and #402 were already re-triaged on `2463257` by the triager (draft PR #414). Not repeated.

### Cells (global mode, Linux)
- pass: `scan -g` (report only) lists globally installed direct packages on pnpm 7.33.7, 8.15.9, 9.15.9, 10.34.5, 11.27.0 and 12.8.1. `-g` inside a project doesn't leak project packages, and a scan without `-g` never reads the global dir. `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` and `--global-prefix $(pnpm root -g)` behave the same as `-g`.
- pass: `scan -g --mode hosted` refuses ("global installs have no project lockfile to redirect"), exits 2 and writes nothing.
- pass: `scan -g --mode agent`, `get -g`, `apply -g`, `rollback -g` (byte-exact) and `vex -g --product …` on direct global deps, pnpm 7.33.7–12.8.1. `vex -g` omits a copy that was manually reverted (`not_applied`).
- **fail #362 (commented)**: transitive deps of global packages are invisible on pnpm 7–10, because the default `-g` layout records `virtualStoreDir: ../.pnpm`. The same happens on pnpm 11, where `-g` uses the global virtual store by default. PR #365 fixes pnpm 7–10 `-g` and leaves pnpm 11 out by design. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/362#issuecomment-5926439290
- **fail #435 (new, regression)**: pnpm 12.4.2, 12.8.1 and 12.8.2, and 11.28.3 with `enableGlobalVirtualStore: false`. Each `pnpm add -g` gets its own `global/v11/<hash>/node_modules/.pnpm`. When two groups both hold left-pad@1.3.0, `get -g` / `apply -g` patch only one, report success, and `vex -g` attests not_affected while the global tool loads the unpatched copy. The result depends on listing order, and it's deterministic on tmpfs. First bad commit is `b32711f` (#269); `0b4e645` and release 4.0.0 pass. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/435

- blocked: macOS and Windows. There's no probe branch, because `git push --delete bughunt/pnpm/20260930-virtual-store` failed again ("unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet").

### Issues
- Filed #435.
- Commented on #362 and #360. Closed #401.

### False positives ruled out
- "rollback deletes the user's pnpm-workspace.yaml": only a user file that becomes byte-identical to hosted mode's scaffold (`packages: ['.']` plus the appended `trustLockfile: true`) is deleted. That's documented in CLI_CONTRACT.md (upstream restore, npm family).
- `get <uninstalled purl>` reports `success, applied: 1` when another manifest patch applies. The nested apply fails only when *no* entry matches. It's not pnpm-specific, so it wasn't filed; it's noted on #362.
- A `rollback -g` that looked "not byte-exact" came from a fixture polluted by an earlier 4.0.0 `scan` in the same global dir. Clean re-runs are byte-exact.

### Next
1. Global mode on macOS and Windows (corepack and standalone pnpm, `PNPM_HOME` with spaces or unicode), once the stale probe branch is deleted.
2. Re-run the hosted edge shapes against v5 (Rush / subspace locks, peer-suffixed workspace instances, catalogs), using the `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL` / `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` harness.
3. Hosted `--frozen-lockfile --offline` with a warm store that holds the upstream tarball, on pnpm 9–12, plus the `vex` honesty check.
4. Agent mode: `dependenciesMeta.injected`, `package-import-method=clone|copy`, and pnpm 1–6 on Node 16.
5. Re-verify #435 and #362 when PR #365 or a fix lands.

### Re-triage
- Skipped. Main hasn't moved since run 4, which re-triaged #360, #401 (closed), #362 and #435 on `2463257`.

### Cells
- **New shape: pnpm 12 two-document lock.** pnpm 12.8.1 writes `pnpm-lock.yaml` as two YAML documents (an env document holding `packageManagerDependencies` / `@pnpm/exe.*`, then the project lock) whenever `package.json` has `packageManager`. pnpm 11.28.3 and 10.34.5 write a single document for the same input.
  - pass: hosted `scan --mode hosted` pins the entry in document 2. A fresh dead-registry frozen install lands the patched bytes, `vex` attests `not_affected`, and `rollback` restores the lock byte for byte. It needs `manage-package-manager-versions=false`, or a reachable registry for pnpm itself.
  - **fail #466 (new)**: vendored on the two-doc lock refuses with `vendor_lock_entry_not_found`. A project vendored first and turned two-doc later breaks on every unwind. `vendor --revert` exits 0 with `success`, rollback reports `vendoredKept` "left untouched", and the default `scan` takeover exits 0 having deleted the ledger. All three leave 5 `file:.socket/vendor` refs, so the next frozen install fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`. Root cause: `section_bounds` takes the first `packages:` / `importers:` header. Reproduced 2/2, and the single-doc control passes. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/466
- pass (VEX honesty): hosted followed by `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile [--offline]` over an existing upstream `node_modules` and warm store, on 9.15.9 / 10.34.5 / 11.28.3 / 12.8.1. pnpm 9 keeps the upstream tree, and pnpm 10 and 11 `--offline` fail with `ERR_PNPM_NO_OFFLINE_TARBALL`. `vex` emits no statement whenever the installed bytes are unpatched, and attests `not_affected` only when the marker is present.
- blocked: macOS and Windows. `git push --delete` of the stale probe branch was denied by the session's permission policy, so no new probe branches were pushed (they couldn't be cleaned up).

### Issues
- Filed #466.

### False positives ruled out
- Hosted on pnpm 9 plus an existing `node_modules`: the frozen install keeps the upstream bytes. That's documented in the `redirect_pnpm_trust_lockfile` warning ("existing node_modules or a warm pnpm store can still contain upstream files"), and VEX doesn't attest it.
- 4.0.0 vendored on the two-doc lock fails with `no_local_source` against the v5-shaped mock. That's a mock incompatibility, so it can't be used for a bisect.
- pnpm 12 warns `The "pnpm" field in package.json is no longer read … pnpm.overrides` on vendored projects. The workspace-file override is what takes effect, so this is noise only. Noted on #466.

### Next
1. Two-doc lock, part 2: pnpm 10.x / 11.x `configDependencies` (does an env document appear there?), and two-doc plus a `packages/*` workspace in hosted mode.
2. Global (`-g`) mode on macOS and Windows, once a maintainer deletes `bughunt/pnpm/20260930-virtual-store`.
3. Hosted v5: Rush / subspace locks, peer-suffixed workspace instances, catalogs.
4. Agent: `dependenciesMeta.injected`, `package-import-method=clone|copy`, pnpm 1–6 on Node 16.
5. Re-verify #435, #362 (PR #365), #400 and #402 (PR #414) when they land.

### Cells
- **fail #518 (new):** in a Rush repo (pnpm 9.15.9 lock 9.0, and 8.15.9 lock 6.0), the npm crawler skips `common/temp` (`SKIP_DIRS` has `"temp"`). Transitive deps installed in `common/temp/node_modules/.pnpm` therefore show as `notInstalled`. After `scan --mode hosted` pins `common/config/rush/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `vex` attests `not_affected` from the lockfile basis while the installed store copy is still upstream. On plain pnpm in the same state, `vex` correctly says `not_applied`. Agent `apply` for the same transitive dep reports `package_not_installed`. Direct deps pass. Reproduced 2/2. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/518
- pass: hosted on Rush. `scan --mode hosted` pins the Rush lock with `redirect_rush_repo_state_stale`. With `preventManualShrinkwrapChanges: true`, `rush install` refuses until `rush update`, as documented. The pin survives `rush update`. A cold `rush install`, a warm one, and `rush install --purge` all install the patched bytes. `vex` attests correctly once the tree is patched.
- **fail #492 (comment):** pnpm 7.33.7 with `shared-workspace-lockfile=false` writes no root lock at all. Hosted then exits `success` / `redirected: 0` with only `redirect_pnpm_no_lockfile`, and the member lock stays unpinned. Reproduced 2/2. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/492#issuecomment-5943308968
- pass: legacy layouts. Agent apply and rollback on a transitive dep (Node loads the patched copy), plus hosted pin → fresh frozen install with an empty store → byte-exact rollback, all pass on:
  - pnpm 2.25.7 (`shrinkwrap.yaml`, `node_modules/.registry.npmjs.org/…`)
  - pnpm 3.8.1 (lock 5.1, same layout)
  - pnpm 4.14.4 (lock 5.1, `.pnpm/registry.npmjs.org/<name>/<ver>`)
  - pnpm 5.18.10 (lock 5.2)
  - pnpm 6.35.1 (lock 5.3)
- pass: agent apply and rollback on peer-suffixed instances (`use-sync-external-store@1.2.0` under react 17 and 18) on 9.15.9 / 12.8.1. Both copies are patched and both are restored.
- pass: npm aliases (`isnum: npm:is-number@7.0.0`). Agent mode passes on 9 / 12. Hosted passes on 7 (lock 5.4), 8 (6.0), 9, 11 and 12: the fresh frozen install is patched.
- pass: hosted with `dependenciesMeta.injected` on 8.15.9 / 12.8.1.
- blocked: hosted injected on 9.15.9. pnpm 9.15.9's own frozen install fails on the *unmodified* lock ("importer dependencies meta (undefined) doesn't match…"), which is an upstream pnpm bug.
- blocked: macOS and Windows. Deleting `bughunt/pnpm/20260930-virtual-store` was denied by the permission policy again, so no probe branches were pushed.

- Filed #518. Commented on #492.

### False positives ruled out
- pnpm 9.15.9's frozen install failing with injected workspace deps reproduces without socket-patch, so it's upstream.
- `rush update --full` drops the hosted pin, because it re-resolves the lock. That's like `pnpm update`, and VEX then honestly reports nothing to attest.

Reproduced 2/2 on 9.15.9, 10.34.5 and 12.8.1. It's the same `find_by_purls` path as npm's #356. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/356#issuecomment-5946785960

- pass: **patchedDependencies interplay**. Two shapes: a pnpm patch on a different file (README.md), and one on the same file (index.js).
  - Agent apply / rollback on the `_patch_hash=` instance passes on 7.33.7 / 8.15.9 / 9.15.9 / 10.34.5. On 11.28.3 / 12.8.1 it only ran without the pnpm patch, because pnpm 11+ ignores `package.json` `pnpm.patchedDependencies`. The same-file shape overwrites pnpm's change with `content_mismatch_overwritten`, which is documented.
  - Hosted on 8.15.9 / 9.15.9 / 10.34.5 / 11.28.3 / 12.8.1 (workspace-file `patchedDependencies` on 11+) passes for both shapes: the lock pin lands, and a fresh frozen install from an empty store gets both the Socket patch and the pnpm patch.
  - `vex` attests `not_affected` for the different-file shape. For the same-file shape it declines with `no_applicable_patches`, because the installed file matches neither hash. That's conservative and honest.
  - Hosted rollback restores the lock.

- pass (documented): hosted on 11.28.3 / 12.8.1 with an explicit `trustLockfile: false | False | no | 'false'`. The setting is respected, the warning names it and gives the remedy, and the frozen install fails (or on 11, `'false'` / `no` installs patched). This matches the CLI_CONTRACT "explicit user settings preserved" rule.
- pass: agent transitive apply / Node load / rollback, with the store kept pristine, on 7.33.7 / 10.34.5 / 11.28.3 for `package-import-method=copy`, `package-import-method=hardlink`, `node-linker=hoisted`, and an npm alias under the isolated linker (12 cells).
- pass (documented refusal): vendored on pnpm 5.18.10 (lock 5.2) and 6.35.1 (lock 5.3) fails loudly with `vendor_lockfile_version_unsupported` and writes nothing.
- pass: vendored on 7.33.7 (lock 5.4) and 8.15.9 (lock 6.0):

  - Same-path frozen install is patched, and `vex` attests `not_affected`.

[agent] 2026-10-02: handover from the Bun bug-hunt routine (ledger #306)

**Finding (low severity, generic to pnpm-shaped stores, not filed):** agent-mode `apply` on a workspace whose member links into the isolated store reports each member-linked package twice. It applies once, then reports a spurious `already_patched` skip for the same real path, so the `--json` summary inflates `skipped`.

- pnpm 10.28.0, main `203e092`, Linux. Root `is-odd@3.0.1`, member `packages/a` → `is-number@6.0.0` + `left-pad@1.3.0`. Run `scan --mode agent`, then `rm -rf node_modules packages/a/node_modules && pnpm install --offline`, then `apply --json`: `applied: 3, skipped: 2`. The 2 skips are `already_patched` for is-number and left-pad, the member's symlinked deps. A second `apply` gives `skipped: 5` for 3 patches.
- Bun 1.4.2 with the isolated linker has the identical shape (`applied: 4, skipped: 3`). The hoisted layout gives `applied: 4, skipped: 0`.
- The bytes are correct; only the event/summary counts are wrong. Likely the apply resolver visits the member's `node_modules/<pkg>` symlink target and the store entry as two locations with the same realpath. No existing issue found.

comments.author: github-actions
comments.body:
[agent] Handover from the npm bug-hunt routine (#302): agent mode writes through workspace links into first-party source

Filed as **#626** (pm:npm): https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/626

With npm, agent-mode `scan`/`apply` follows a `node_modules/<name>` symlink that points at a workspace member, a `file:` directory or an `npm link` target whenever that local package's `name@version` matches a patched registry package. The default mismatch policy then overwrites the user's own `index.js` with the upstream patched file. `vex` attests it, and `rollback` writes the upstream *original* over the user's code. Vendored mode refuses the same case (`vendor_workspace_member`).

The suspect code is shared by the whole npm family: `crates/socket-patch-core/src/crawlers/npm_crawler.rs:1933` `acceptable_package_entry` accepts any symlink in an importer tree. pnpm links `workspace:` deps and `link:` / `file:` dirs the same way, so the pnpm routine may want to check:
- a pnpm workspace member named `left-pad`, version `1.3.0`, depended on via `workspace:*`
- a `link:../fork` dependency

with `socket-patch scan --mode agent` against a mock patch for `left-pad@1.3.0`. If it reproduces, add a comment to #626 rather than filing a duplicate.

Repro script (npm): see the issue body.

- An offline frozen install into an empty store fails while any unpatched dependency exists (already a known non-bug).

2. Rush subspaces (`common/config/subspaces/*`), and Rush + pnpm 8 / 10.

### Re-triage

### Cells
- **fail #696 (new):** hosted `vex` with pnpm `modulesDir` (backlog item 2 from run 12). On pnpm 10.12+ the virtual store moves to `<modulesDir>/.pnpm`. The crawler misses it, and the manifest-less "nothing installed → attest from the lock pin" rule then reports `not_affected` (exit 0) while the installed copy is upstream. It fails on 10.12.0 / 10.34.5 / 11.28.3 / 12.8.1 (3–4 times each) and passes on 9.15.9 / 10.11.1 and with the default modules dir. Release 4.0.0 is honest. Bisected first bad: `cf8150b` (#251). https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/696
- **fail #696 (comment):** the same false attestation for **transitive** deps under `enableGlobalVirtualStore: true` and under a `virtualStoreDir` outside the project (11.28.3 / 12.8.1, twice each). Pass: an in-project `virtualStoreDir: .vstore` transitive (10.34.5 / 12.8.1), and a GVS direct dep (`not_applied`, exit 1). https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/696#issuecomment-5969470682

Rollback restores the upstream `resolution` byte-exactly and keeps the `patch_hash` snapshot and `patchedDependencies`. A fresh frozen install into an empty store gets upstream bytes plus the user's pnpm patch. Before rollback, `vex` honestly declines (`hash_mismatch`).

- Release 4.0.0 `vex` exits 2 (`manifest_not_found`) on a v5 hosted checkout, because it has no ledger to read. That isn't a comparison point for GVS/vsd.

- **#636 comment:** a vendored → hosted takeover with 2 packages leaves the same `pnpm.overrides: {}` and vendored workspace scaffold. Hosted mode then appends `trustLockfile: true` to that scaffold, so a full `rollback` can no longer delete it (8.15.9 package.json only; 9.15.9 / 10.34.5 / 12.8.1 package.json + 4-line workspace file; reproduced 2× on 12). The final lock is byte-exact, `.socket` is deleted, and no `pnpm` table is left (`remove` doesn't hit #636). Backlog item 4 is done.

Fresh frozen installs on 8 / 9 / 10 / 11 / 12 are patched: `semver` and `esbuild` bins work, optional `@esbuild/linux-x64` is patched, `fsevents` is skipped on Linux, and transitive tarball-URL pins work on 11 / 12.
