[agent] 2026-10-05 (06:43 UTC): pnpm bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `045d7ec` (unchanged since run 11), latest release 4.0.0 (installed from npm for the regression check). Linux only, Node 22, pnpm 7.33.7 / 8.15.9 / 9.15.9 / 10.34.5 / 11.28.3 / 12.8.1. I rebuilt the local Python mock of the patch API (batch, by-package, view with inline blobs, package grant, hosted tarball under `/patch/npm/<name>/<ver>/tok/<uuid>/…`, `/registry/<name>/<ver>` mirror). It serves patches for `left-pad@1.3.0`, `Base64@1.3.0`, `JSONStream@1.3.5`, `jsonparse@1.3.1`, `debug@4.3.4` and `ms@2.1.2`.

### Re-triage
- Main hasn't moved and no pnpm fix has merged (open fix PRs: #598, #605, #634, #672, #698, #802, #810, and #818 for #557), so I didn't re-run the open set.

### Cells (each failure reproduced at least twice)
- **fail #830 (new): vendored parent + vendored dependency** (`debug@4.3.4` → `ms@2.1.2`; also `JSONStream` → `jsonparse`). Reverting the parent splices its pre-vendor snapshot block back over the child's live `file:` ref.
  - `remove pkg:npm/debug@4.3.4` exits 0, but the next frozen install fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` on 7.33.7 / 8.15.9 / 9.15.9 / 10.34.5 / 11.28.3 / 12.8.1.
  - The vendored → hosted takeover reports `success` / exit 0 with `ms` skipped as `vendored_revert_failed`, yet `ms` is already un-vendored and isn't pinned, so a fresh frozen install gets unpatched `ms` (7–12). CLI_CONTRACT requires `redirect_takeover_unpatched` / `partial_failure` / exit 1 for this.
  - `rollback` exits 1 forever (lock already byte-exact, `ms` artifact and ledger stranded; 7–12). `vendor --revert` leaves the same residue with exit 0 (9 / 12).
  - Controls: `remove pkg:npm/ms@2.1.2` (the child) passes. Hosted mode with the same pair passes (`remove` parent → frozen install patched, rollback byte-exact; 9 / 12).
  - Not a regression: release 4.0.0's `remove` leaves the same broken lock (9 / 12).
- pass: **mixed-case package names** (`Base64`, `JSONStream`; pnpm 9+ stores them as `.pnpm/Base64@1.3.0_<hash>`):
  - hosted pin + fresh frozen install patched + `vex` attests, on 7.33.7 / 8.15.9 / 9.15.9 / 10.34.5 / 11.28.3 / 12.8.1;
  - agent apply patched on every version;
  - vendored patched on 9–12; on 7 / 8 it's patched in place (a moved checkout is the documented absolute-`file:` limitation);
  - hosted rollback byte-exact on 8 / 9 / 12.
- pass (fails closed): vendored with a user parent-selector override (`JSONStream>jsonparse: 1.3.1`) on 9 / 10 refuses `jsonparse` with `vendor_override_conflict` and `vex` omits it. Hosted pins all copies.
- pass (fails closed): vendored with a user range-selector override (`left-pad@<2: 1.3.0`) on 9 / 10 / 12 refuses with `vendor_override_conflict`, writes nothing, and `vex` finds nothing to attest.
- pass: agent mode with `symlink=false` (empty root `node_modules`) and `hoist=false` on 9 / 10 / 12. Direct and transitive copies are patched.
- pass: `list -g` (text and `--json`) on pnpm 11.28.3 and 12.8.1 global installs.
- pass: agent apply and `list` with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` on 9 / 12.
- fail #661 (existing, not commented): pnpm 10.34.5 with `modules-dir=deps` only in the global `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pnpm/rc` gives agent `applied: 0` with exit 0. Open PR #698 already handles it by probing `.modules.yaml`. pnpm 12.8.1 ignored `modulesDir` in the global `config.yaml` (installed into `node_modules`).
- pass: a hosted scan SIGKILLed mid-run (during the grant request) leaves no residue. The lock is untouched, and the re-run succeeds.
- blocked: macOS and Windows. Deleting the stale probe branch `bughunt/pnpm/20260930-virtual-store` was denied by the permission policy again, so I pushed no new probe.

### Issues
- Filed #830: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/830

### False positives ruled out
- An API that answered with lowercased purls (`pkg:npm/base64@1.3.0` for an installed `Base64`) made the in-run agent summary claim `applied: 3` with two packages unpatched. Standalone `apply` honestly reports `package_not_installed`. There's no evidence the real API lowercases npm names, and the summary inflation isn't pnpm-specific (see the known non-bug about `get` + `applied`), so I didn't file it.
- `scan -g --mode agent` also patched npm's own bundled `jsonparse` under `/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/npm`. The npm global root is in `-g` scope, so this isn't pnpm-specific. On pnpm 11's global virtual store that copy made `jsonparse` look `already_patched` while the GVS copy stayed pristine (the #362 GVS transitive gap). Fixture note: `-g` runs touch the sandbox's npm install.
- The vendored `vendor_override_conflict` detail for a parent-selector override says "an exact-version pin equal to 1.3.1 is taken over automatically" even though the exact pin isn't taken over (it's a selector). The pnpm 12 range-selector detail names "package.json's `left-pad@1.3.0`" when the overrides live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. Both are cosmetic; the refusals are correct.

### Next
1. #830 follow-ups: a three-level chain (a → b → c, all vendored), `scan --mode vendored` re-run over the broken `remove` state (does it heal?), and the pnpm 7/8 workspace dialect.
2. Re-verify the open set (#360 #362 #435 #466 #492 #556 #557 #590 #601 #626 #627 #633 #636 #661 #662 #696 #713 #714 #734 #754 #756 #778 #830) when fixes land.
3. #778 follow-ups: pnpm 7 workspace layout.
4. `list` under Rush (`common/config/rush/pnpm-lock.yaml`).
5. macOS / Windows probes (global mode, #754), once the stale probe branch is deleted.

[agent] 2026-10-05: handover from the Yarn classic (1.x) bug-hunt routine

I filed #831 (https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/831) for yarn classic. Vendored mode writes `.socket/vendor/npm/<uuid>/<name>-<ver>.tgz` and never probes git ignores. With an ordinary `.gitignore` rule, the scan still exits 0 with no warning, the commit drops the tarball, and every fresh-checkout frozen install fails:
- `*.tgz` (GitHub's stock Node.gitignore)
- `vendor/`
- `.socket/`

With `vendor/` or `.socket/` ignored, `state.json` is dropped as well, and `vendor --check` exits 0 (`discovered: 0`) while the lock still points into `.socket/vendor`. Only the vlt backend has the `vendor_artifact_gitignored` probe (`vlt_lock.rs:762`) and the `<uuid>/.gitignore` `!*` re-include.

The tarball backends look like they share this, but I haven't tested pnpm. Please check it with a real pnpm install (repro shape in #831). If it reproduces, comment on #831 with your matrix rather than filing a duplicate, unless the fix clearly differs.

- Filed #854: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/854
- Commented on #831: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/831#issuecomment-5994647930

- **`yarn remove` of a vendored package, then rollback / remove / `vendor --revert`: fail #665** (1.7.0 / 1.22.22). Hosted same flow: pass.

### Run 12 cells (`045d7ec`)
- **Vendored workspaces, installs from a member dir (`cd b && yarn install --frozen-lockfile`, `yarn --cwd b install`, `yarn workspace b add`), cold cache: fail #691** on Linux / macOS / Windows × 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 (probe run 37123949202). Root installs pass. Warm-cache member installs pass (masking).
- **Vendored block merged by yarn with a second range (`a@^1.1.0, a@^1.3.0:`) → rollback / remove / `vendor --revert`: fail #692** (Linux 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22). Re-vendor says `already_vendored` and doesn't re-key.
- `yarn add`/`yarn upgrade` that re-keys or re-resolves the vendored block: the #665 shape (fix in flight, #689).

### Run 13 cells (Linux, `045d7ec`)
- Hosted with a merged key created after the scan → rollback: pass (1.22.22). Hosted isn't affected by #692.
- Vendored #692 shape: `vendor --check` reports OK and `repair` is a no-op while rollback fails: fail #692 (commented).
- Merged key already present before vendoring, V + frozen install + rollback byte-exact: pass (1.22.22).
- Scoped merged key: H frozen install on 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 pass; V on 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 pass (rollback byte-exact); H⇄V takeover chain + re-run + rollback pass.

### Run 14 cells (Linux, `045d7ec`)
- Fork alias `"left-pad": "npm:async@1.3.0"` and the yarn-merged `left-pad@1.3.0, "left-pad@npm:async@1.3.0":` block, H/V/A: all fail-closed, pass (1.22.22).
- agent → hosted takeover + rollback: pass. **agent → vendored takeover + rollback / remove / `vendor --revert`: fail #336** (node_modules left patched, record dropped, yarn's next frozen install is "Already up-to-date"). 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22.
- #591 shape: `vendor --check` OK and `repair` no-op: fail #591 (commented).
- `yarn.lock` + `package-lock.json` together, H and V: pass. Hosted `vex` before reinstall: `not_applied`, pass. `--link-duplicates` agent apply / vex / rollback: pass.

### Run 15 cells (Linux, `045d7ec`)
- **Bundled copy (`bundledDependencies`) of the patched name@version beside the normal copy: fail #758.** The scan gives no warning. The hosted in-run `--vex` attests, and vendored in-run and post-install `vex` attest, while the bundled copy stays unpatched. Hosted post-install `vex` and agent mode are correct. 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22.
- `get <uuid> --mode hosted|vendored|agent` (project mode) + frozen install + vex: pass. `list` (H / V / A / CRLF+BOM merged-key workspace / `--json`): pass (1.22.22).
- `scan --mode vendored --prune` after `yarn remove`: entry kept (`keptVendoredEntries`), fail #665 (PR #689 covers the prune path).
- Vendored odd range keys merged into one block (hyphen, `||`, `>= <`, `v`-prefix) + frozen install + rollback byte-exact: pass. 20k-block lock hosted scan: 2.9 s, pass.
- vendored → agent → reinstall → `apply` → rollback → frozen reinstall: pass (1.22.22).

### Run 16 cells (`045d7ec`)
- **Windows path shapes** (probe, windows-latest, yarn 1.10.1 / 1.22.22; H/V scan + fresh frozen install + rollback, A apply + vex + rollback): a >MAX_PATH project path (345 chars), a directory-junction project dir, a `subst` drive (`--cwd X:/p` from another drive, and run inside `X:\`), cross-drive `--cwd` both ways, a backslash `--cwd`: all pass. yarn on Windows writes CRLF locks natively (`os.EOL`), and H/V rollback restores them byte-exact.
- Linux: CRLF H/V + rollback (1.0.2 / 1.6.0 H; 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 H+V), H⇄V takeover chain on 1.7.0 and BOM+CRLF on 1.10.1, V offline mirror on 1.9.4 / 1.17.3, `yarn add` (1.7.0) then rollback, a lock-only workspace with an alias, conflict markers around the target (fail-closed), a missing vendored artifact (`vex` omits it): all pass. Also a 414-char path and a symlinked project dir.

### Run 17 cells (`045d7ec`)
- **Cross-OS vendored checkout portability** (probe run 37226728998, yarn 1.22.22): a project vendored on Linux, macOS or Windows, then installed `--frozen-lockfile --offline` (cold cache), `vendor --check`, `vex --offline`, `list` and rollback on each of the three OSes. All 9 cells pass, with rollback byte-exact (CRLF for a Windows producer). Windows writes forward-slash `file:./.socket/…` paths.
- A 4-package project (prerelease `ms@3.0.0-canary.1`, dotted `lodash.isequal`, scoped `@types/left-pad`, `left-pad`): H pass on 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22, V pass (byte-exact rollback) on 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22, A (apply + vex + rollback) pass on 1.6.0 / 1.7.0 / 1.9.4 / 1.17.3 / 1.22.22.
- Private-registry `resolved` URLs (Verdaccio `%2f`, Nexus, a URL with no `.tgz` basename), H and V: pass. A vendored grant without `sha1`: vendored computes `#sha1`, and the warm-cache install is patched (not #558). A tampered vendored tarball → check fails, vex omits it, repair restores: pass. Vendored re-run idempotent, and V→H→V: pass. `get <purl>` for prerelease / scoped purls (`%40` or `@`): pass.

### Run 18 cells (`045d7ec`)
- **macOS + Windows probe** (run 37248870997; yarn 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22): project agent apply + vex + rollback + re-run, pass. V + offline mirror + pruning (fresh offline frozen, in-place offline, byte-exact rollback, post-rollback offline install), pass. agent → vendored takeover + rollback: **fail #336** on all 6 cells (commented).
- Linux warm-cache H / V / A (+ V / A rollback) on 1.12.3 / 1.13.0 / 1.15.2 / 1.16.0 / 1.18.0 / 1.19.2 / 1.21.1: pass.
- Multi-hash `integrity "sha1-… sha512-…"` target block, H / V: pass. Lookalike same-version blocks (`@evil/left-pad`, `my-left-pad`) untouched: pass. Hosted workspace member-dir frozen installs (`cd member`, `--cwd member`): pass.

### Run 19 cells (Linux, `045d7ec`)
- **Vendored + `.gitignore` covering the artifact** (`*.tgz`, `vendor/`, `.socket/`), then commit, fresh clone and frozen install: **fail #831** on 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. The scan exits 0 silently. With `vendor/` or `.socket/` ignored, `vendor --check` in the clone also exits 0.
- Vendored + `.gitattributes` `* text eol=lf` / `* text=auto eol=crlf`: pass (1.22.22). `* text eol=crlf` corrupts the `.tgz` (see Known non-bugs).

### Run 20 cells (Linux, `4646693`)
- #363 verified fixed on real yarn: git-only dep, H (1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.22.22) and V (1.7.0 / 1.22.22), lock untouched, frozen installs OK, nothing attested: pass.
- **Hosted pin beside a git sibling (workspace registry + `git+…` copies): rollback / remove / list refuse, the takeover skips the restore, and `vendor --revert` lands on hosted: fail, #828 (commented)** on 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. Pure vendored on the same shape: pass.
- **Vendored git-only dep: misleading `vendor_lock_entry_not_found` and the git warning dropped: fail #857** (1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22).
- #758 still reproduces (1.10.1 / 1.22.22). Run-18 battery (agent, V + mirror) on `4646693`: pass. #336 still fails.
- GitHub shorthand after #710: blocked (no codeload access in the sandbox).

## Backlog

1. Re-check #364 (PR #839) / #831 (PR #837) once merged, and #828's yarn git-sibling shape once fixed. Then #467 / #519 / #558 / #591 / #627 / #691 / #692 / #758 / #857.
2. Hosted-git shorthands (`owner/repo`, `github:`, `bitbucket:`, `gitlab:`) after #710, via a probe (the sandbox can't reach codeload).
3. Cross-OS hosted checkout: embed one prebuilt patched tarball (base64) in the probe so every runner serves identical bytes. Add workspaces to the cross-OS vendored probe.
4. #758 follow-ups: a real registry package with `bundledDependencies`.
5. **Maintainer request (global mode), what's left:** the Windows MSI install of yarn, and a read-only prefix on Windows with a non-admin user. #437 (1.0.x) is still open. macOS case-insensitive name collisions. Same-size patched files on yarn ≤1.9 in-place installs.

## Known non-bugs

- `patches-api.socket.dev` isn't used here. Use a local mock API (`--api-url`). The mock must match purls with an unencoded `@` for scoped packages, and vendored runs need `--vendor-source build` plus `blobContent` in the view stub. For hosted `vex` on lock-only checkouts, pass `--patch-server-url <mock>` (CLI_CONTRACT "Patch hosts"); otherwise `package_not_found` is expected.
- **yarn 1.0.2 – 1.6.x install nothing (exit 0, empty node_modules) for `file:` tarball lock entries and offline-mirror installs, even without socket-patch.** Bisected in run 2: Node 10.24.1 / 14.21.3 / 16.20.2 / 22 all behave the same, and 1.7.0 works on all of them. The cause is in yarn, not Node or socket-patch, which is why CI reports `KNOWN LIMITATION` for vendored ≤ 1.6. Not in docs/ecosystems.md.
- An `npm:` alias entry is left unpatched in hosted mode with `redirect_yarn_classic_alias_skipped` (documented), and `vex` omits the package.
- A BOM plus no yarn header comment makes the first entry `entry_not_found`. Yarn always writes the header, so this is synthetic.
- `file:` directory and `link:` deps are skipped by design. (`file:` **tarball** deps are rewired and work.)
- The GitHub shorthand `owner/repo#tag` locks as a codeload tarball and is correctly rewired; only `git+…` patterns are #363.
- Running `scan` from a workspace member dir: vendored → `vendor_lockfile_missing` (exit 1); hosted → exit 0, `redirected: 0`, `redirect_npm_no_lockfile` (npm-only wording). This is the documented hosted refusal posture.
- hosted→agent / vendored→agent keep the existing wiring (`hosted_wiring_retained` / `vendored_ownership_retained`), as documented.
- Concurrent scans: the extras fail with `lock_held` (intended).
- Probe branches can't be deleted from the sandbox (the git proxy rejects ref deletion). Leftovers: `bughunt/yarn-classic/20260930-mirror-git`, `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261001-win-crlf-git`.
- **v5 hosted `rollback` / `remove` need the npm registry.** In the sandbox the CLI's rustls client rejects the TLS-intercepting proxy CA (`error sending request for url (https://registry.npmjs.org/…)`). That's a sandbox artifact. Use a local plain-HTTP registry passthrough with `env -u HTTPS_PROXY -u https_proxy SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. With `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` set, the restored `resolved` uses `dist.tarball` verbatim (registry.npmjs.org), not registry.yarnpkg.com. That's by design (`npm.rs` `yarn_classic_tarball`).
- v5 vendored mode has no local build (`--vendor-source build` is rejected). The mock must serve a `tarball` artifact from `POST …/patches/package`.
- `scan -g` also reports npm's own bundled deps (npm global root), e.g. `@isaacs/string-locale-compare`. That's correct global discovery.
- Probe branch `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261001-global-mode` is also left on the remote (the proxy blocks deletion).

- Hosted pins are recognized only on `patch.socket.dev` or the `--patch-server-url` / `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL` origin. With a mock at another origin and no such setting, `rollback` says `Manifest not found` (truly-empty project). Set `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL=<mock>`.
- Hosted rollback of a lock without `integrity` lines (yarn < 1.10) adds `integrity` lines. That's the "default upstream entry", and yarn 1.7 still installs it frozen.
- Vendored mode on yarn ≤ 1.6 installs nothing. The harness asserts this as a KNOWN LIMITATION (`tests/common/yarn_classic_vex.rs:89`); it's not in the user docs.
- A tarball-URL dependency of the patched name@version is rewired in both modes (it installs patched). Whether a URL "fork" should be refused, as vlt does, is a design question.
- A SIGKILL can leave the lock wired with no `vendor/state.json`. `rollback` then refuses with a remedy, and `repair` / a re-scan rebuild the ledger. That's intended crash handling.
- Hosted rollback ignores the `.yarnrc` `registry` and queries `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` (default registry.npmjs.org). That's documented (CLI_CONTRACT Hosted unwind / env table). Set `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` behind a private registry.
- A nested non-workspace project (its own `yarn.lock` under the root) in hosted mode from the root: `redirect_yarn_classic_entry_not_found`, because hosted reads only the root lock. That's the documented one-project model (run with `--cwd` per project).
- A stale `node_modules` left beside an active `--modules-folder`: Node loads `node_modules` first, so agent patching it is correct.
- Yarn classic never sends `.npmrc` registry auth (host token, bare `_authToken`, `always-auth`, scoped registry, `_auth`) to the hosted patch host, on any release from 1.0.2 to 1.22.22. The berry #404 leak doesn't apply to classic.
- Vendored `vex` attests from the committed artifact even when the installed tree is unpatched (by design, with a `vendored_tree_out_of_sync` warning).
- `scan --vex` in a PnP project exits 1 `manifest_not_found` only because there is nothing to attest. Plain `scan` exits 0 with `yarn_pnp_unsupported`, as pinned by `e2e_safety_yarn_pnp.rs`.
- A platform-skipped optional dep (`fsevents` on Linux) is rewired and attested from the lock pin in hosted mode: the documented lock-only basis, and it installs patched on macOS.
- The mock harness must exclude `node_modules` relative to the package dir, or it serves empty tarballs (a harness bug, not socket-patch).
- yarn classic ignores `YARN_MODULES_FOLDER` / `npm_config_modules_folder` (installs into `node_modules`), so the crawler needn't read them. A `~/.yarnrc` `--modules-folder` resolves relative to `$HOME`, not the project.
- v5 has no `setup` subcommand. Agent cells use `apply`.
- Probe branch `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261002-dev-flow` is also left on the remote (the proxy blocks deletion).
- An `npm:` alias key merged with a direct key in one block isn't something yarn 1.22.22 writes (it emits two blocks), so don't test that shape.
- Hosted rollback on an `integrity sha1-` lock restores a sha512 `integrity` line (the default upstream entry); yarn 1.10 installs it frozen.
- `patch.socket.dev` / `patches-api.socket.dev` are blocked by the sandbox egress proxy, so what the real grant carries (e.g. whether `sha1` is present) can't be checked from here.
- yarn 1.0.x–1.9.x in-place installs skip copying a file whose size and mtime match the installed one (yarn's copy optimisation). With same-length markers and mtime-0 mock tarballs, a superseded patch looks unapplied in place. Fresh installs and 1.10+ are fine. Use different-length markers in harnesses.
- A `.yarnrc` modules-folder that is absolute, or that resolves outside the project, is deliberately ignored by the crawler (fail-closed, `npm_crawler.rs` `resolve_modules_folder`).
- The local mock's batch route must filter by the requested purls, or `scan -g` "finds" packages it never inventoried.
- **macOS probe harness:** the first TCP connects to a freshly started Python mock on a macOS runner stall for 10–30 s. Before #581 the first `scan -g` simply took ~35 s. Since #581's 10 s connect bound, those batches fail (`api_batch_failed` / "All N API batch queries failed", exit 1). This is a harness artifact: warm the mock with a `curl` loop before the first scan. Once warm, `-g` report / agent / vex pass on macOS.
- Agent mode patches a `link:` / `yarn link` dependency's target directory, even outside the project. That's the code Node loads; whether to refuse it is a design question.
- Leftover probe branches (deletion blocked): `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261003-global-rerun`, `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261003-macos-global`.
- A symlinked `.socket/` or `.socket/vendor/npm` in a *single* project works consistently in vendored mode (writes and cleans up at the link target). Only a store shared between projects is #664.
- `vex -o` is `--org`, not `--output`. Use `--output` in harnesses.
- Hosted rollback after `yarn remove` of a patched package: pass (restores the remaining blocks, removes `.socket/`).
- Leftover probe branch (deletion blocked): `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261003-member-install`.
- Quick vendored harness: a scratch cargo test using `tests/prebuilt_common` `prepare_command` (auto-mocks the service for `vendor`/`repair`) plus a staged `.socket/manifest.json` + blob, as in `e2e_vendor_yarn_classic_dev_flow.rs`. Other commands (rollback / remove / `vendor --revert` / `--check`) run offline with the plain binary.
- A plain root `yarn add <pkg>@<new range>` re-resolves a vendored block from the registry (unpatched). That's yarn's own behaviour; the follow-on rollback is #665.
- A vendored lock after a hosted→vendored takeover, rolled back, restores `registry.npmjs.org` (the hosted-unwound entry, via `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY`), not the original `registry.yarnpkg.com`. Documented; frozen installs are fine.
- Agent-mode mock: serve `GET /v0/orgs/<org>/patches/blob/<hash>` for both the before and the after hash. `…/patches/diff/<uuid>` may 404 (it falls back to blobs). Without the before blob, rollback reports `missing_blob`.
- `vex` in a workspace root whose `package.json` has no `version` exits `product_undetected`. Pass `--product`.
- yarn classic itself merges `left-pad@1.3.0` into an existing `left-pad@npm:async@1.3.0` block (it installs the fork for the real name). That's a yarn bug; socket-patch fails closed on that block in all modes.
- With `yarn.lock` and `package-lock.json` both present, hosted rewrites both (and writes `.npmrc` allow-remote), and vendored wires `yarn.lock` with `vendor_multiple_lockfiles`. Intended.
- After `yarn remove` of a vendored package, `list` still shows the entry as "recorded in .socket/vendor/state.json". That's accurate about the ledger; the cleanup gap is #665.
- Rebuilt the mock in run 15: the public-proxy path also calls `GET /patch/by-package/<purl>` (a `SearchResponse` with the patch summary) before `/patch/view/<uuid>`. Without it, scan says "could not fetch patch details".
- **Windows probe harness:** Git-Bash `sed` drops CR bytes, so a `sed`-normalised copy of yarn's CRLF lock never equals the original. Compare locks with raw `cmp`. Git-Bash also can't exec a program from a cwd longer than MAX_PATH; run `yarn --cwd <long path>` from a short dir.
- yarn 1.x on Windows writes *new* lockfiles with CRLF (`os.EOL`, `writeFilePreservingEol`), and keeps an existing file's EOL. CRLF locks are therefore the default on Windows, not an edge case.
- Running `scan --mode agent` from a workspace member dir finds nothing ("No packages found"), because the hoisted copies live under the root. That's the documented one-project model: run from the root.
- Leftover probe branch (deletion blocked): `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261004-win-paths`.
- **Probe harness:** `actions/upload-artifact` drops dot-directories (`.socket/`) unless you set `include-hidden-files: true`. A per-runner Python mock builds tarballs with that OS's zlib, so hashes differ across OSes. Ship one shared mock artifact for hosted cross-OS tests.
- `get name@version` (not a purl) runs the fuzzy package-name search, and against the mock it returns `no_packages`. Use a `pkg:` purl or a uuid.
- Leftover probe branch (deletion blocked): `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261004-xos-vendored`.
- Agent mode never crawls a workspace member under `vendor/`, `build/`, `dist/`, `tmp/`, `temp/`, `coverage/`, `__pycache__/` or a hidden dir (e.g. `.github/actions/*`), even when yarn `workspaces` declares it. That's the documented walk (docs/ecosystems.md "npm: which node_modules trees are crawled"); whether declared workspaces should override it is a design question.
- Leftover probe branch (deletion blocked): `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261005-agent-xos`.
- **Self-contained mock (run 18):** one Python file serving `left-pad@1.3.0` for all modes (batch, by-package, view with `blobContent`, `…/package` grant with a sha512+sha1 tarball artifact, `/artifacts/<uuid>/…`, `blob/<hash>` for before and after). It lives in the run-18 probe workflow on `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261005-agent-xos`.
- A `.gitattributes` `* text eol=crlf` (forced text for every file) corrupts the vendored `.tgz` on checkout. The same setting corrupts every binary in the repo, so it's not filed; `vendor --check` reports it (`vendor_artifact_unreadable`). vlt guards it with a `<uuid>/.gitattributes` `* -text`, and the tarball backend doesn't. `* text=auto …` and `* text eol=lf` are fine.
- #363 / #664 / #665 were closed by #710 / #666 / #689. Don't re-file the git-rewire shape; a git block is now skipped by design (docs/ecosystems.md "yarn classic git dependencies").
- yarn 1.0.2 installs a single copy (the git one, at the root) for a workspace that has both a registry block and a git block of the same `name@version`. The hosted pin then never reaches `node_modules`, but the scan's `redirect_yarn_classic_git_skipped` warning covers it and `vex` doesn't attest.
- The sandbox can't reach codeload.github.com, so GitHub-shorthand deps need a probe branch.

comments.body:
[agent] 2026-09-30: Yarn classic (1.x) bug-hunt run

This is the first run, so the ledger started empty and there were no `pm:yarn-classic` issues to re-triage.

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9` (CLI 4.0.0; latest release 4.0.0, also used to check for regressions). Yarn via corepack: 1.0.2, 1.6.0, 1.7.0, 1.9.4, 1.10.1, 1.17.3, 1.22.22 on Node 22 (Linux sandbox). One probe run covered ubuntu, macOS and Windows × 1.10.1 and 1.22.22.

**Setup:** I used a hold-open Python mock of the patch API (batch / by-package / package / view with `blobContent` / hosted tarball in the production URL shape) and patched tarballs built from the real `npm pack` tarballs. Every cell ended with a real `yarn install` on a fresh checkout and a patch-marker check.

## Cells

- **Hosted baseline** (1.0.2, 1.6.0, 1.10.1, 1.22.22; fresh `--frozen-lockfile`): pass.
- **Hosted + `yarn-offline-mirror`:** **fail → #364.** On 1.10+, an online install hits "Integrity check failed" because the mirror's upstream `left-pad-1.3.0.tgz` has the same basename as the hosted URL. `--offline` fails on 1.7+. Linux, macOS and Windows all fail. On 1.7.0 and 1.9.4 an online install passes. 1.0.2 and 1.6.0 are n/a, because they install nothing from a mirror even without socket-patch.
- **Vendored + offline mirror** (1.10.1, 1.22.22; online and `--offline`): pass.
- **Hosted + vendored with a git-sourced dep** (`git+file://…#v1.3.0`): **fail → #363.** The block is rewritten, and yarn then runs git against the tarball, so every install fails ("Command failed" / "spawn ENOTDIR"). The in-run VEX says `not_affected`. Fails on Linux 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 and macOS 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. Windows is blocked (the fixture install couldn't find git).
- **`file:` directory dep:** skipped by both modes, pass. **Remote tarball URL dep:** rewired and installs patched, pass.
- **Hosted workspaces + merged ranges (`^1.3.0`, `1.3.0`, `~1.3.0`) + `resolutions` + scoped package + `npm:` alias** (1.22.22): pass. The alias is skipped with `redirect_yarn_classic_alias_skipped` (documented), and `vex` correctly omits left-pad because of the unpatched alias copy.
- **Vendored, same project** (1.22.22, 1.7.0): pass. It rewires the alias too, and all copies are patched.
- **Hosted CRLF / BOM / BOM+CRLF / headerless locks, then `rollback`** (1.22.22): pass, byte-exact restore.
- **Vendored CRLF / BOM+CRLF, then `vendor --revert`**: pass, byte-exact.
- **Hosted in-place warm reinstall** (1.0.2, 1.10.1, 1.22.22): pass.
- **Re-run idempotency** (hosted and vendored): pass (lock unchanged).
- **Agent `scan --apply` + `setup` postinstall hook, then `yarn add` / `--check-files` / reinstall** (1.0.2, 1.10.1, 1.22.22): pass.
- **Agent mode on nested workspace copies** (version conflict + `nohoist`): pass.

## Issues

- Filed #363: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/363
- Filed #364: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/364

## False positives ruled out

- Scoped packages at first looked "not redirected". That was my mock URL-encoding `@` in purls; the CLI sends it unencoded.
- yarn 1.0.2 and 1.6.0 "exit 0 but nothing installed" from an offline mirror: this happens without socket-patch too (yarn / Node 22), the same family as CI's `KNOWN LIMITATION` for `file:` tarballs on ≤ 1.6.
- A lock with a BOM and **no** yarn header comment misses its first entry (`redirect_yarn_classic_entry_not_found`). Yarn always writes the header, so the lock is synthetic and not filed.
- GitHub-hosted git specs couldn't be fetched through the sandbox proxy, so I used a local `git+file://` repo.

## Probe branches

- `bughunt/yarn-classic/20260930-mirror-git`, run https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36761888480 (6/6 jobs green; the results are in the RESULT lines).
- **Couldn't delete the branch.** `git push origin --delete` fails through the session git proxy ("remote end hung up"). Sibling routines' probe branches are also still on the remote. A maintainer needs to delete `bughunt/*/2026*` branches.

## Next

[agent] 2026-10-01: maintainer note: test global (`-g`) mode for hosted patches

This is a maintainer request, not a run report. Add it to the top of the backlog and keep it there until the cells below are covered.

**Ask:** make sure we correctly scan global installs when `-g` / `--global` is passed, on every major Yarn classic (1.x) version and on Linux, macOS and Windows.

**Where Yarn classic (1.x) puts global installs:** `yarn global add`; discovery via `yarn global dir`. Cover a custom `--global-folder` / `prefix` in .yarnrc, and yarn installed via npm, corepack and the Windows MSI.

**What to check** (prove each with a real global install, not by reading source):
1. `socket-patch scan -g` (no `--mode`) is report-only. It must find every globally installed Yarn classic (1.x) package that has a hosted patch: none missing, no project packages leaking in, correct versions. Also check `--json`.
2. `scan -g` run from inside a Yarn classic (1.x) project versus outside one: `-g` must scan only the global location, and a scan without `-g` must never touch it.
3. `scan -g --mode hosted` and `scan --global-prefix <dir> --mode hosted` must refuse loudly, as designed ("global installs have no project lockfile to redirect"). They must exit non-zero and write nothing.
4. `get -g` defaults to agent mode. Check `scan -g --apply`, `apply -g`, `rollback -g` and `vex -g`: the globally installed copy is actually patched (run the installed tool or import it), rollback restores it byte for byte, and `vex` only attests what's applied.
5. `--global-prefix <dir>` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behave the same as `-g`. That covers custom prefixes, version managers, paths with spaces or unicode, and a non-root user's prefix.
6. A global directory you can't write to (root-owned prefix, Windows Program Files) must fail loudly with a clear error, never exit 0 unpatched.

Add OS × Yarn classic (1.x) version cells for `-g` (scan report / apply / rollback) to the coverage matrix, and use probe branches for macOS and Windows.

Hosted `rollback` now re-resolves the upstream entry from the npm registry, and the CLI's rustls client doesn't trust the sandbox's TLS-intercepting CA, so `error sending request` here is a **sandbox artifact**. Work around it with a local plain-HTTP passthrough and `env -u HTTPS_PROXY -u https_proxy SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. With that env set, the restorer writes `dist.tarball` verbatim (registry.npmjs.org) instead of registry.yarnpkg.com, which is expected.

- #363 (git-sourced blocks rewired): **still reproduces** on v5. New: hosted `rollback` reports success but "restores" the git block to the registry tarball, so installs keep failing. Comment: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/363#issuecomment-5926333522
- #364 (hosted + offline mirror): **still reproduces** on 1.22.22 (`Integrity check failed`). I had nothing new to add, so I didn't comment.

- **v5 hosted `rollback` (upstream restore)** on a 3-dep lock (plain, scoped and is-number), 1.22.22: **pass**. Exit 0, all 3 reverted, and the lock is byte-exact apart from the registry host (an artifact of the env above).
- **Global mode (maintainer checklist)**, `yarn global add left-pad is-number`:
  - `scan -g` report-only finds the yarn-global packages, both inside and outside a project. There's no leakage either way: a scan without `-g` reports only the project, and the project lock is untouched. **pass** on Linux / macOS × 1.10.1 / 1.22.22.
  - `scan -g --mode hosted`, `--global-prefix … --mode hosted` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1 --mode hosted` all exit 2 and write nothing: **pass** on every OS and version.
  - `scan -g --mode agent` / `get <uuid> -g` patch the real global copy (`require()` works), `vex -g` attests only the applied copies (dropping one manually removes it from subcomponents), and `rollback -g` / `--global-prefix` rollback are byte-exact. `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behaves the same. **pass** on Linux (sandbox + CI) and macOS × 1.10.1 / 1.22.22.

  - Read-only global folder (`sudo chown root` + `chmod -R a-w`, runner user): exit 1 `partial_failure`, left unpatched, **pass** on Linux / macOS × 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. The sandbox runs as root, so it can't test this.
  - **`get -g --mode hosted|vendored` and `scan -g --mode vendored` → filed #436.** They rewrite the cwd project's yarn.lock, exit 0 and leave the global copy unpatched. Reproduces on all 3 OSes × 1.0.2 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. v4.0.0 behaves the same, so it's not a v5 regression.
  - **yarn 1.0.x → filed #437.** `yarn global dir` doesn't exist before 1.1.0 (bisected: 1.0.2 fails, 1.1.0+ works), so yarn-global packages are silently missed on every OS.
  - **Windows, every yarn → commented on #434** (pm:npm, the bare `yarn` spawn never resolves `yarn.cmd`). `scan -g`, agent apply, vex and `SOCKET_GLOBAL` all fail on 1.10.1 / 1.22.22.

- Filed #437: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/437
- Commented on #363: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/363#issuecomment-5926333522
- Commented on #434: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/434#issuecomment-5926458034

- My first local "yarn 1.0.2 / 1.10.1" global runs actually used a system yarn 1.22.22, because of a PATH mistake in my harness. I discarded them and re-ran with the shim.

[agent] 2026-10-01: Yarn classic (1.x) bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `2463257` (unchanged since the last run), latest release v4.0.0. Linux sandbox only, Node 22, yarn 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 from `npm i yarn@<v>` shims. I used no probe branches: every cell this run is pure lock-text handling and OS-independent, and the open Windows/global issues (#434 → PR #442, #436 → PR #446) haven't merged yet.

**Harness for the next run (v5):** a Python mock that serves `POST /patch/batch`, `GET /patch/view/<uuid>`, `POST /patch/package` (a `granted` tarball artifact with sha512/sha1/md5/sha256) and `GET /artifacts/…`. Point both `SOCKET_API_URL` and `SOCKET_PROXY_URL` at it (not `SOCKET_PATCH_PROXY_URL`), and set `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL=<mock>`. **Without that last one, hosted pins aren't recognized and `rollback` correctly says `Manifest not found`.** Hosted rollback uses the plain-HTTP registry passthrough + `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` from earlier runs. `vex` on a nameless root package.json needs `--product`.

## Re-triage
- No new commits on main since the last run, so #363 / #364 / #436 / #437 are unchanged. I added no comments. Fix PRs are open for #436 (#446) and the Windows spawn (#442).

## Cells (Linux, v5 `2463257`)
- **Mixed CRLF+LF yarn.lock** → **fail, filed #467.** Hosted converts every LF line in the file (untouched blocks included) to CRLF. Vendored splices the rewired block with the file's dominant ending (`detect_eol`) instead of `block_eol`. In both modes `rollback` isn't byte-exact. Yarn install and `check --integrity` still pass, so severity is low.
- Uniform CRLF and BOM+CRLF locks: hosted→vendored and vendored→hosted takeovers, frozen install patched, rollback: **pass** (CRLF and BOM preserved; the only diff is the passthrough's registry host).
- `--dry-run` (scan in hosted / vendored / agent, plus `rollback --dry-run`) on CRLF / BOM+CRLF / mixed locks: **pass**, byte-identical, nothing created.
- Vendored v5 service artifacts on workspaces + multi-version (`left-pad@1.3.0` / `~1.2.0`), merged key `is-number@7.0.0, is-number@^7.0.0`, and an `npm:` alias: **pass**. All copies are patched, 1.2.0 is untouched, and the alias is vendored. `vex` attests both, `vendor --check` and `repair` succeed, a frozen `--offline` install works, and rollback is byte-exact with `.socket/` removed. Hosted on the same project: **pass** (alias skipped with `redirect_yarn_classic_alias_skipped`, as documented).
- Vendored + `yarn-offline-mirror` + pruning on 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 (v5): **pass**. A frozen offline install from an empty cache is patched, rollback is byte-exact, and after rollback it reinstalls unpatched from the mirror.
- Locks from yarn 1.7 (no `integrity`): hosted and vendored, frozen install on 1.7.0 and 1.22.22: **pass**. Hosted rollback adds `integrity` lines the original lacked, and 1.7.0 still installs frozen, so this is harmless (see non-bugs).
- Direct tarball-URL dependency (`"left-pad": "https://…/left-pad-1.3.0.tgz"`): hosted and vendored rewire it and the frozen install is patched: **pass**. (Design question, not filed: a URL "fork" tarball with the same name@version would be replaced by Socket's patched upstream; vlt refuses that shape.)
- `file:` directory dep in hosted mode: left untouched, `Not hosted … no lockfile entry pinning it could be rewritten`, `vex` doesn't attest it: **pass**.
- Interrupted runs: SIGKILL at random points in 35 vendored and 20 hosted scans. Every state installs. One state is wired + tarballs present + **no ledger**: `rollback` refuses loudly with a remedy, and `repair` or a re-scan rebuilds the ledger, after which rollback is byte-exact. A stale `.socket/apply.lock` doesn't block the next run: **pass**.

## Issues
- Filed #467: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/467

## False positives ruled out
- Hosted `rollback` "Manifest not found": the mock origin wasn't the recognized patch host. `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL` fixes it (CLI_CONTRACT "Hosted unwind coverage", Scope).
- An offline vendored install failing on a workspace with an unpatched `left-pad@1.2.0`: my empty cache didn't hold the registry tarball. That's a test artifact.
- Vendored mode on yarn ≤ 1.6 installs nothing: a known limitation the test harness asserts (`tests/common/yarn_classic_vex.rs:89`). Worth a docs note, but not filed.

## Next
1. Global-mode Windows cells once #442 / #446 merge (then re-test #434 / #436 / #437).
2. `socket.yml` filters and `--max-new-patches` on a yarn workspace. `optionalDependencies` / platform-skipped packages in both modes and vex.
3. `.yarnrc` `--install.frozen-lockfile true`, `--pure-lockfile`, `yarn import` locks.
4. Custom `registry` in `.yarnrc` (private mirror `resolved` hosts) through hosted → rollback: is the restored host acceptable to a frozen install behind the mirror?
5. Probe macOS/Windows for #467 only if a fix lands (string handling, OS-independent).

- The stale `node_modules` + `--modules-folder` "false VEX": Node's resolution order loads the patched `node_modules` copy.

**macOS + Windows probe** (branch `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261005-agent-xos`, run [37248870997](https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/37248870997); macos-latest / windows-latest × yarn 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22):
- Project-mode agent: `scan --apply --mode agent`, `vex`, `rollback` (byte-exact `index.js`), then an agent re-run. **pass** on all 6 cells. These fill the "A apply" cells that were untested on macOS and Windows.
- Vendored + offline mirror + `yarn-offline-mirror-pruning`: a fresh `--frozen-lockfile --offline` install from an empty cache, an in-place `--offline` reinstall (pruning), rollback (byte-exact lock, CRLF on Windows), then a post-rollback offline install from the mirror (unpatched). **pass** on all 6 cells. These fill the "V offline mirror" cells that were untested on macOS and Windows.
- agent → vendored takeover → rollback → `yarn install --frozen-lockfile`: **fail #336** on all 6 cells. yarn says "Already up-to-date" and node_modules stays patched. I commented on #336 with the cross-OS table.

**Linux:**
- Warm-cache H / V / A on intermediate releases 1.12.3 / 1.13.0 / 1.15.2 / 1.16.0 / 1.18.0 / 1.19.2 / 1.21.1: the scan, then a frozen reinstall from the same (upstream-warmed) cache installs patched bytes. V and A rollback are byte-exact, and a V post-rollback frozen install is unpatched. **pass** (21 cells).
- A multi-hash `integrity "sha1-… sha512-…"` line on the target block: H and V rewrite it to a single sha512, the frozen install is patched and V rollback is byte-exact. **pass**
- Lookalike blocks with the same version (`"@evil/left-pad@^1.3.0"`, `my-left-pad@1.3.0`): left untouched by H and V. **pass**. An alias-only block is skipped by H (documented warning) and rewired by V (as before).
- Hosted workspaces: a fresh frozen install run from a member dir (`cd packages/b && yarn install --frozen-lockfile`, `yarn --cwd packages/a install --frozen-lockfile`) installs patched bytes. **pass** (hosted isn't affected by #691).

## Issues
- Commented on #336 (yarn classic leg on macOS and Windows): https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/336#issuecomment-5986321701
- No new issues filed. None closed.

## False positives ruled out
- A workspace member that lives under `vendor/`, `build/`, `dist/`, `tmp/`, `temp/`, `coverage/` or a hidden dir (e.g. `.github/actions/*`) is never crawled in agent mode, so its non-hoisted copy isn't patched. That's the documented walk (docs/ecosystems.md "npm: which node_modules trees are crawled"), so I didn't file it. Declared yarn `workspaces` globs aren't consulted, and whether they should be is a design question.
- Hosted rollback exited 1 in the sandbox. That's the known rustls/proxy registry artifact (Known non-bugs); I didn't re-run it through a passthrough.

## Probe branch
I couldn't delete `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261005-agent-xos` (the git proxy rejects ref deletion). A maintainer needs to delete it.

## Next
1. Re-check #363 (PR #710), #665 (PR #689), #664 (PR #666) and #627 (PR #802) once they merge, then #364 / #467 / #519 / #558 / #591 / #691 / #692 / #758.
2. Cross-OS hosted checkout: embed one prebuilt patched tarball (base64) in the probe so every runner serves identical bytes.
3. #758 follow-ups: a real registry package with `bundledDependencies`.
4. A Windows directory junction as `.socket/vendor/npm` (#664 shape), after #666.
5. Global-mode leftovers (Windows MSI yarn, a non-admin read-only prefix). macOS case-insensitive name collisions.

Harness: yarn bundles come from npm `@yarnpkg/cli-dist@<v>` (`node package/bin/yarn.js`), because corepack's fetch can't use the sandbox proxy. Yarn 4 needs `YARN_HTTPS_CA_FILE_PATH`; yarn 2/3 need `YARN_CA_FILE_PATH`. The npm registry has 2.4.2 as the last 2.x in cli-dist. Agent and vendored cells hand-stage `.socket/manifest.json` plus blobs (a marker prepended to `index.js`). Hosted cells use a local Python mock (fresh-checkout copies must keep `.socket/` for vendored cells) of the patch API (batch, by-package, `patches/package` with a `yarn-berry-zip` `yarnBerry10c0` artifact, `view`, and the tarball route). The 10c0 checksum is bootstrapped with a real yarn `resolutions: file:` install. Every hosted and vendored cell ends in a fresh-checkout `yarn install --immutable`. v5: hosted rollback/remove need the mock's `/upstream/npm/<uuid>.json` route, `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` pointed at a local registry passthrough (the rustls binary can't use the sandbox proxy CA), and `--patch-server-url <mock>` so the pins count as hosted. Global (`-g`) cells use real npm global installs (`NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX`) and a Python mock of the authenticated API (`--api-url <mock> --api-token x --org org`; blob route `/v0/orgs/org/patches/blob/<sha256>`). v5 vendored mode downloads from the vendoring service: the same mock's `/patches/package` with a granted `tarball` artifact (real sha512) is enough, and an optional per-patch `status` override (for example `pending_build`) is supported. ## Backlog

1. **Blocked on a maintainer:** probe-branch deletes fail (runs 10–13 and 20: `send-pack: unexpected disconnect` / `remote end hung up`; runs 14 and 19: denied by the session permission policy), so no new probes. The stale branches `bughunt/yarn-berry/20260930-builtin-patch-takeover` and `bughunt/yarn-berry/20261001-global-script` need deleting by hand. After that, probe the resolutions pin on macOS and Windows (CRLF), plus #539, #632, #859.
2. Re-verify when fixes land: #859 (relocated pnpm store), #831 (Berry), #783 (then `@scope/parent/name`, a scoped target, the hosted→vendored takeover), #759, #737 (#719 did not fix it), #632 (PR #763), #539, #628/#629. Fixed and verified in run 20: #697, #718, #817 (and its takeover variant), #665 Berry. #368, #369, #370, #404, #440, #468, #495 and #559 are closed.
3. #859 neighbours: `pnpmStoreFolder` outside the project (`../shared`, shared by two projects: does agent mode patch every project's copy?), and `YARN_NODE_LINKER`/`YARN_PNPM_STORE_FOLDER` via env only (#634's rc-only check may refuse direct deps).
4. #719 renderer edge cases: string `bin` on a scoped package, empty-string bin values (yarn drops them), a served tarball whose top dir isn't `package/` (the hosted fetch reads only `package/package.json` → `npm_manifest_unavailable`).
5. #831 follow-ups once fixed: the `<uuid>/.gitignore` `!*` re-include under `*.tgz`, and the hosted→vendored takeover under an ignore rule.
6. Berry analogue of #664 (a symlinked `.socket/vendor/npm` shared by two projects); #666 has landed.
7. Global (`-g`) on macOS/Windows, and a version-manager prefix (nvm/volta). Full checklist in the 20261001T040000Z entry.
8. Unconfirmed lead: the API returns a lower-cased npm purl (`pkg:npm/jsonstream@1.3.5`) for a mixed-case package, and every mode misses it. File it (cross-PM) only if the real API is shown to lower-case.
9. Hosted `vendor --check`/`vex` drift after a user drops the pin. Re-check Berry on #725 once PR #730 merges.

## Known non-bugs

- Yarn 2/3 (cacheKey 7/8) are refused by hosted and vendored mode (documented).
- PnP projects with a `.pnp.cjs` are refused in every mode with `yarn_pnp_unsupported` (documented).
- Vendoring a package yarn builtin-patches (`resolve`, `typescript`, `fsevents`) is refused fail-closed with `vendor_override_conflict`. It's loud and closed, so it isn't filed (the hosted counterpart is #368).
- Hosted refuses an entry that merges a direct descriptor with an `npm:` alias (`"left-pad@npm:1.3.0, lp@npm:left-pad@1.3.0"`) with `redirect_yarn_berry_ambiguous_entry` and exit 1. It's fail-closed and loud; arguably over-broad, but not filed.
- Agent mode: a later `yarn install --immutable` in the same tree doesn't restore unpatched bytes (yarn's install-state), and the setup hook re-patches after a clean install. Standalone `vex` in agent mode needs `setup` or `setup.manual` (documented).
- `patches-api.socket.dev` is unreachable from the sandbox; use the mock.
- A BOM'd yarn.lock fails `yarn install --immutable` (YN0028) on its own, because yarn strips the BOM. Not caused by socket-patch.
- Hosted on a berry `npm:` alias-only entry → `redirect_yarn_berry_alias_skipped` (documented in docs/ecosystems.md).
- `scan <workspace-member-dir>` finds 0 packages: hosted/vendored PATHs are project dirs, and members share the root's lock (CLI_CONTRACT "exclude it with ignorePackages, not paths").
- PnP with `.pnp.cjs`: scan reports 0 packages with a PnP warning (same in 4.0.0). A PnP lock-only checkout gets hosted pins, and those install correctly under PnP.
- v5 rollback/remove/list treat only `patch.socket.dev` (or `--patch-server-url`) URLs as hosted pins. Without that flag, a mock host reads as "Manifest not found".
- PnP on yarn 2.x (`.pnp.js`) and 3.x is detected and gets the loud PnP warning in every mode, exit 0 (same as 4.x).
- An agent-mode re-run (`scan -g --mode agent`) after a failed apply (EACCES) exits 0 with "already recorded … run `socket-patch apply`". This is the designed re-run message; `apply -g` itself exits 1.
- The report-only hint after `scan -g` doesn't mention `-g`. It's cross-PM and was handed to npm (#302), so it isn't filed here.
- Yarn 4 hardened mode (`enableHardenedMode`, auto-on for public fork PRs in GitHub Actions) accepts a hosted `::__archiveUrl=` lock pin, as does `--check-resolutions` (4.12.0, registry reachable).
- Zero-install (`enableGlobalCache: false` with `.yarn/cache` committed): hosted mode is lock-only, so the committed cache keeps the unpatched zip, and `yarn install --immutable --immutable-cache` fails YN0056 until `yarn install` refreshes the cache. Vendored mode behaves the same way (the `file:` entry has no cache zip; no warning). It's a docs gap, not filed.
- `compressionLevel` set outside the project `.yarnrc.yml` (env, home or parent rc) can't cause a wrong checksum: yarn bakes the level into the lock's `cacheKey`, which both modes gate on.
- Vendored refuses a user `yarn patch` (`patch:` descriptor) with `vendor_override_conflict`, plus an alias-only dependency (root or workspace member) with `vendor_lock_entry_not_found`, a merged direct + alias entry, and a user-authored `resolutions` key for the target. All are loud and closed with nothing written, so none are filed.
- Mixed CRLF/LF `yarn.lock` is refused by vendored (`vendor_yarn_berry_mixed_line_endings`) and hosted (`redirect_yarn_berry_mixed_line_endings`). That's correct: yarn itself fails YN0028 on such a lock.
- v5 `rollback` drops the patch's manifest entry, so a later `apply` is a no-op (designed).
- A berry install rewrites a BOM'd, compact, or no-trailing-newline `package.json`. Vendored snapshots the post-install bytes and reverts to them byte-exactly.
- Vendored refuses a lock that resolves the target name at a second version (`left-pad@1.2.0` alongside the patched 1.3.0) with `vendor_override_conflict`, because the name-keyed `resolutions` would move both. That's correct and loud.
- `repair` refuses (`vendor_artifact_redownload_failed`, nothing written) when the service now serves different bytes for a uuid whose integrity is pinned in the ledger. That's correct.
- `vendor --cwd <workspace member>` fails loudly with `vendor_lockfile_missing` (the lock lives at the root).
- Yarn 4 locks carry no `virtual:` entries for peer-dependent packages, so the hosted/vendored rewrite has no virtual locator to keep in sync.
- Hosted rollback reformats a compact one-line `package.json` to 2-space and drops a user-authored empty `"resolutions": {}`. Yarn's own next install writes exactly the same bytes, so it isn't filed.
- Hosted per-package refusals (`redirect_yarn_berry_shared_descriptor`, `redirect_yarn_berry_ambiguous_entry`, `cache_unsupported`) exit 0 with `redirected: 0` and nothing written. With `--vex` and nothing to attest, the run exits 1.
- Hosted refuses a user-authored `resolutions` entry targeting the patched package (bare or scoped selector) with `redirect_yarn_berry_resolutions_conflict`. It's documented and loud.
- An interrupted (SIGKILL) vendor can leave a ledger + tgz without the package.json/yarn.lock wiring. A re-run completes, `vendor --revert` removes the orphan, and `vex` refuses. `rollback` and `repair` fail with `manifest_not_found` in that state.
- After a hosted pin, a user descriptor change (`yarn add left-pad@1.3.0`) leaves a stale `resolutions` selector. `rollback` in that state refuses loudly and tells you to re-run `scan --mode hosted`, which re-pins correctly. It's fail-closed and gives a remedy, so it isn't filed.
- #628 (hosted rewrites a mixed-EOL root package.json) was filed by the arch audit; don't re-file it.
- Hosted on a direct tarball-URL descriptor (`left-pad@https://…tgz`) is refused with `redirect_yarn_berry_unsupported_protocol`, exit 0, nothing written. That's correct.
- `compressionLevel: mixed` (cacheKey `10`) is refused by hosted (`redirect_yarn_berry_cache_unsupported`, exit 0) and vendored (`vendor_yarn_berry_cache_unsupported`, exit 1). Both are documented.
- Hosted on a user `patch:` descriptor in `dependencies` is refused (`redirect_yarn_berry_unsupported_protocol` + `redirect_yarn_berry_shared_descriptor`), nothing written. That's correct. The hint suggests `--mode vendored`, which also refuses it; `--mode agent` works.
- Yarn 4 writes no `checksum:` for a platform-conditional entry reached only through `optionalDependencies`, and strips one on its next mutable install. A hosted pin's checksum on such an entry therefore doesn't survive `yarn add`; `vex` still attests from the installed tree. That's yarn's policy. The misplaced-line part is #697.
- A hosted pin whose `bin:` differs from the tarball's passes a plain `yarn install --immutable` and a later mutable install (yarn trusts the locked entry). Only hardened mode or `--refresh-lockfile` fails, and that is #718.
- A scoped patch missing from a mock-driven scan is a mock artifact if the mock doesn't fully unquote `%2540` purls (run 14).
- `lockfileFilename` in `.yarnrc.yml` is rejected by yarn 4 ("Unrecognized or legacy configuration settings"). It only exists in yarn 2/3, which hosted/vendored refuse anyway.
- `checksumBehavior` (ignore/update/reset) doesn't change what yarn writes to the lock. Hosted and vendored pins pass under all three (run 15).
- A user `**/name` resolution is dropped from `package.json` by yarn 4's own install, so a hosted pin that seems to replace it isn't socket-patch's doing (run 16).
- `compressionLevel:` with its value on the next line (a multi-line YAML scalar) is refused by both modes. It's loud and unrealistic, so it isn't filed (run 16).
- Vendored `vex` on a tree whose `node_modules` still holds unpatched bytes (wiring pulled without a reinstall) attests `not_affected` from the committed artifact and warns `vendored_tree_out_of_sync`. That's by design (run 17).
- `vendor --check` reporting wiring verified after the Berry wiring drifts is #725 (cross-PM root cause, Berry evidence commented in run 17). Don't re-file it.
- `yarn install --mode=update-lockfile` (Renovate) still writes `checksum:` lines on yarn 4.0.2 and 4.18.1, so there are no checksum-less target entries to test (run 18).
- A hosted-rollback bare `npm:<v>` locator where yarn wrote `::__archiveUrl=` passes hardened mode and `--refresh-lockfile`. The breakage is only the fetch (#817).
- `scan --mode agent --json` reporting an apply failure as `action: "added"`, `failed: 0` with no error is #424 (cross-PM, open). Don't re-file it (run 20).
- Yarn 4.0.x rejects `pnpmStoreFolder` ("Unrecognized or legacy configuration settings"), so #859 cells start at 4.1+ (run 20).

[agent] 2026-09-30: Yarn Berry (2+) bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9` (CLI 4.0.0 workspace version), latest release 4.0.0 (previous 3.3.0, both from npm for comparison). Yarn 2.4.2, 3.8.7, 4.0.2, 4.12.0 and 4.18.1 (the current `latest`) from `@yarnpkg/cli-dist`, on Node 22. Patch data is a hand-staged `.socket/manifest.json` plus blobs (agent and vendored mode) and a local Python mock of the patch API with a bootstrapped `10c0` checksum (hosted mode). No secrets.

This is the first run: no earlier ledger, and no `pm:yarn-berry` issues to re-triage.

### Cells
- **fail #368**: hosted `scan --mode hosted` of `resolve@1.22.8` / `typescript@5.4.5` (packages yarn builtin-patches, `optional!builtin<compat/…>`). It exits 0 with success and VEX `not_affected`, and then every fresh `yarn install --immutable` fails YN0028. Linux on 4.0.2, 4.12.0 and 4.18.1; macOS and Windows probe on 4.12.0 and 4.18.1. Release 4.0.0 has the same bug.
- **fail #369**: the hosted→vendored takeover (`vendor`) reverts the hosted redirect, then per-package vendoring refuses (`vendor_override_conflict`: a second left-pad version in a workspace). The package ends up unpatched in both modes. Linux, macOS and Windows; release 4.0.0 has the same bug.
- **fail #370**: `compressionLevel: 0 # comment` in `.yarnrc.yml` is refused as a non-default compression level, in vendored and hosted mode (4.12.0, 4.18.1; release 4.0.0 too).
- pass, vendored (4.12.0): root, scoped root workspace name, scoped target, `**/` glob resolution present, workspaces (member dep), pnpm linker, re-run idempotent (`already_vendored`), `--revert`, in-place `--immutable` install after vendor. 4.18.1: CRLF-respelled lock + package.json.
- pass, hosted: left-pad on 4.0.2 / 4.12.0 / 4.18.1 (fresh `--immutable` gets the patched bytes); pnpm linker + standalone `vex`; rollback byte-exact (lock + package.json), including after a `resolve` redirect; Windows CRLF locks (probe).
- pass, agent: `apply` / `rollback` on node-modules and pnpm linkers (byte-exact); `setup` postinstall hook re-patches on a clean install; `setup --remove` byte-exact.
- refused, as designed: yarn 2.4.2 / 3.8.7 (cacheKey 7/8) in hosted and vendored; PnP with `.pnp.cjs` (`yarn_pnp_unsupported`); vendoring a builtin-patched package (`vendor_override_conflict`); hosted with a merged direct + `npm:` alias entry (`redirect_yarn_berry_ambiguous_entry`).

### Issues
- Filed #368, #369 and #370.

### False positives ruled out
- The first probe run (36763523523) failed because of my harness, not the product. GH runners set `CI`, so yarn made the fixture install immutable; also, Windows tar parses `D:\…` as a remote host. Fixed in the rerun.
- Agent-mode `rollback` "failing" was a fixture without the before-blob. With the blob staged, it's byte-exact.
- An agent-mode `yarn install --immutable` in the same tree keeping the patched bytes is yarn's install-state behaviour, not a socket-patch problem.

### Probe
- `bughunt/yarn-berry/20260930-builtin-patch-takeover`, run https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36764922521 (ubuntu, macos and windows × yarn 4.12.0 and 4.18.1). **The branch could not be deleted:** `git push --delete` got "remote end hung up" three times, and the REST ref delete returned 403. A maintainer needs to delete it.

### Next
1. Yarn 2/3 agent and vendored cells; `get --mode hosted|vendored` front doors.
2. Zero-install `.yarn/cache` interplay (`--immutable-cache` after hosted or vendored), and PnP lock-only checkouts with no `.pnp.cjs`.
3. The vendored→hosted takeover mirror of #369, and whether yarn classic / npm share the per-target takeover gap.
4. `compressionLevel` from env / home / parent `.yarnrc.yml`, and quoted keys.
5. macOS/Windows cells for vendored and agent mode.

[agent] 2026-10-01: Yarn Berry (2+) bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `2463257` (the v5 consolidation, #277; the CLI still reports 4.0.0), against release 4.0.0 from npm. Yarn 4.0.2, 4.12.0 and 4.18.1 from `@yarnpkg/cli-dist`, on Node 22, Linux only. Hosted cells use a local Python mock of the patch API (batch, by-package, `patches/package`, `view`, the tarball route, and the new v5 `/upstream/npm/<uuid>.json` route). Rollback needs that route plus `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` pointed at a local registry passthrough, because the rustls binary can't reach the registry through the sandbox proxy. Rollback, remove and list need `--patch-server-url <mock>`, or the pins aren't recognised as hosted.

### Re-triage
- #368: **still reproduces** on v5 main (resolve, YN0028). New: user `yarn patch` entries (`patch:…#./.yarn/patches/x.patch`) break the same way for any package. Commented: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/368#issuecomment-5922687885
- #370: **still reproduces** (`compressionLevel: 0 # default` is refused). Commented: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/370#issuecomment-5922688428
- #369: not re-checked. Vendored mode in v5 needs a vendoring-service mock (`--vendor-url`), which isn't built yet.

### Cells
- **fail #404 (new)**: a hosted `::__archiveUrl=` pin makes yarn send the npm registry `Authorization: Bearer` token to the patch host. This happens for scoped packages whenever an `npmAuthToken` / `YARN_NPM_AUTH_TOKEN` / `npmScopes` token is set, and for all packages under `npmAlwaysAuth: true`. Seen on 4.0.2, 4.12.0 and 4.18.1.
- pass, hosted (v5 main): left-pad on 4.0.2 (bare-hex), 4.12.0 and 4.18.1 (lock `version: 10`); a scoped package; CRLF lock + package.json; re-scan idempotent; workspaces with a merged-range entry (`left-pad@npm:1.3.0, left-pad@npm:^1.3.0`); a PnP lock-only checkout (hosted pin, then a fresh PnP install loads the patched bytes).
- pass, v5 manifest-less rollback / remove / list: byte-exact upstream restore on 4.0.2, 4.12.0, CRLF and workspaces (including after a `resolve` redirect); per-purl `remove`; `list` shows the hosted pins; rollback under PnP with `.pnp.cjs` present.
- documented / not a bug: `npm:` alias-only entry → `redirect_yarn_berry_alias_skipped`; `scan packages/a` on a workspace member finds nothing (contract: PATH is a project dir, members share the root's lock); PnP with `.pnp.cjs` → scan reports 0 packages with a PnP warning, the same as release 4.0.0.

### False positives ruled out
- A BOM'd yarn.lock fails `--immutable` YN0028 because yarn itself strips the BOM. It does that on the untouched lock too.
- The first rollback "Manifest not found" came from my harness: the mock host isn't recognised as hosted without `--patch-server-url`.
- 4.18.1 installs against a lock written by 4.12 fail YN0028 (lock `version: 8` → `10`). That's yarn's own migration.

### Probe
- No new probe branch this run. The stale `bughunt/yarn-berry/20260930-builtin-patch-takeover` still can't be deleted (`git push --delete` hangs up again), so **a maintainer needs to delete it**.

### Next
1. Build a vendoring-service mock (`--vendor-url`) and re-run the v5 vendored cells, #369, and the takeovers.
2. Probe branch: #404 token capture on macOS/Windows, and yarn 4.x with `npmRegistryServer` pointing at a private registry.
3. Hosted upgrade path (a superseding uuid for a pinned dep), then rollback through the new uuid's upstream metadata.
4. Zero-install committed `.yarn/cache` after hosted/rollback (stale zips, `--immutable-cache`).

[agent] 2026-10-01: maintainer note: test global (`-g`) mode for hosted patches

This is a maintainer request, not a run report. Add it to the top of the backlog and keep it there until the cells below are covered.

**Ask:** make sure we correctly scan global installs when `-g` / `--global` is passed, on every major Yarn Berry (2+) version and on Linux, macOS and Windows.

**Where Yarn Berry (2+) puts global installs:** Berry has no `yarn global`; `yarn dlx` caches don't persist. Check that `-g` on a Berry-only machine discovers nothing from the project's .yarn/cache or PnP, is clean and loud about it, and still finds the npm/pnpm globals that sit next to it.

**What to check** (prove each with a real global install, not by reading source):
1. `socket-patch scan -g` (no `--mode`) is report-only. It must find every globally installed Yarn Berry (2+) package that has a hosted patch: none missing, no project packages leaking in, correct versions. Also check `--json`.
2. `scan -g` run from inside a Yarn Berry (2+) project versus outside one: `-g` must scan only the global location, and a scan without `-g` must never touch it.
3. `scan -g --mode hosted` and `scan --global-prefix <dir> --mode hosted` must refuse loudly, as designed ("global installs have no project lockfile to redirect"). They must exit non-zero and write nothing.
4. `get -g` defaults to agent mode. Check `scan -g --apply`, `apply -g`, `rollback -g` and `vex -g`: the globally installed copy is actually patched (run the installed tool or import it), rollback restores it byte for byte, and `vex` only attests what's applied.
5. `--global-prefix <dir>` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behave the same as `-g`. That covers custom prefixes, version managers, paths with spaces or unicode, and a non-root user's prefix.
6. A global directory you can't write to (root-owned prefix, Windows Program Files) must fail loudly with a clear error, never exit 0 unpatched.

Add OS × Yarn Berry (2+) version cells for `-g` (scan report / apply / rollback) to the coverage matrix, and use probe branches for macOS and Windows.

Berry turns that into `yarn run global dir`, so it runs the project's `"global"` script and scans whatever directory the script prints as a global install. This reproduces on Linux and macOS with yarn 2.4.2, 3.8.7, 4.12.0 and 4.18.1, under the node-modules and PnP linkers, with `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1`, and on release 4.0.0. It doesn't reproduce on Windows, because `Command::new("yarn")` doesn't resolve `yarn.cmd`. Probe run: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36828589815
- pass: `scan -g` report-only with no `--mode` (finds the global `zz-global-pkg`; `--json` scannedPackages and packages are correct). Run inside node-modules, pnpm and PnP Berry projects, it gives the same result as outside, with no project packages leaking in. `scan` without `-g` never touches the global copy.
- pass: `scan -g --mode hosted`, `scan --global-prefix <dir> --mode hosted` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1 scan --mode hosted` all refuse with exit 2 and write nothing.
- pass: `scan -g --mode agent`, `get -g` (defaults to agent), `apply -g` (idempotent) and `rollback -g` (byte-exact sha256, twice) on the real global copy. `--global-prefix` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL_PREFIX` behave the same, on a path with a space and unicode.
- pass: `vex -g` attests while the patch is applied. After `npm i -g --force` restores unpatched bytes, it omits the package (`not_applied`) and exits 1.
- pass: a root-owned prefix with a non-root user (`setpriv` uid 65534). `scan -g --mode agent` fails loudly (EACCES, exit 1), and so does `apply -g`.
- pass: agent mode on yarn 2.4.2 and 3.8.7 with the node-modules linker (apply, then rollback restores the bytes). PnP on 2.4.2 (`.pnp.js`) and 3.8.7 gets the loud PnP warning in every mode (documented).

### Observations not filed
- A re-run of `scan -g --mode agent` after the EACCES failure exits 0 with "already recorded … run `socket-patch apply`" while the package is still unpatched. It's the designed agent-mode re-run message, the same in project mode, and not Berry-specific.
- The report-only hint after `scan -g` says `socket-patch scan --mode agent [PATHS]` without `-g`, so following it targets the project, not the globals. It applies to every package manager, so it's handed over to npm (#302).
- Windows: `yarn global dir` is never run, because of the `.cmd` shim, so yarn classic's global dir is probably never discovered on Windows. Handed over to yarn-classic (#304).

### Probe branches
- `bughunt/yarn-berry/20261001-global-script` (run 36828589815). **Deletion failed:** the git proxy answers `git push --delete` with HTTP 403. `bughunt/yarn-berry/20260930-builtin-patch-takeover` still can't be deleted either. **A maintainer needs to delete both.**

### Next
1. Global mode, rest of the checklist: macOS and Windows apply/rollback for `-g` (probe), and a version-manager prefix (nvm/volta layout under `$HOME`).
2. Build a vendoring-service mock (`--vendor-url`) and re-run the v5 vendored cells and #369.
3. Probe #404 on macOS and Windows; private `npmRegistryServer` plus `npmAlwaysAuth`.
4. Hosted upgrade path (a superseding uuid) plus rollback through the new uuid's upstream metadata.
5. Zero-install committed `.yarn/cache` after hosted/rollback; `compressionLevel` from env or `~/.yarnrc.yml`.

A `corepack` shim on PATH (`corepack yarn@X` → `node <cli-dist X>/bin/yarn.js`) should let the repo's own berry e2e suites run in the sandbox. It was built but not exercised yet.

- **#369 commented** (https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/369#issuecomment-5932074198). It still reproduces on v5 through `scan --mode vendored` and `get <uuid> --mode vendored` (the hosted pin is restored to the registry, then `vendor_override_conflict`, exit 1, patched in neither mode). `vendor` with no manifest (the v5 eject path) now refuses first and keeps the hosted pin.
- #404 has a fix in flight (draft PR #465, not merged), so I didn't re-run it. #368, #370 and #440 weren't re-run (main is unchanged).

### Cells
- **fail #468 (new)**: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/468. The vendored → hosted takeover reverts the vendored wiring, artifact and ledger, and only then does the berry rewriter skip the package because the grant has no `yarnBerry10c0` (`redirect_yarn_berry_missing_checksum`). The run reports exit 0, `success`, `redirected: 0`, and claims "the project is now fully hosted for this package". After that, a fresh immutable install is unpatched and `vex` says `manifest_not_found`. Reproduces on yarn 4.0.2, 4.12.0 and 4.18.1.
- pass: the vendored → hosted takeover when the grant has the checksum (redirects 1, fresh immutable install patched).
- pass: the vendored → hosted takeover with the hosted reference `pending_build`. It stays vendored and exits 0 with `redirected 0` and no warning, which is quiet but correct.
- pass: the **hosted upgrade path**. A lock pinned to uuid A, with the API now serving uuid B: re-scan re-pins to B, a fresh `install --immutable --check-cache` installs B's bytes, and `vex` attests. Then `rollback` (through B's `/upstream` metadata) restores the pre-hosted registry lock **byte-exact**.
- pass (v5 vendored, first v5 cells): root vendoring with `scan --mode vendored` (`resolutions` `file:` plus the lock entry; fresh `install --immutable --check-cache` patched). A workspace with `^1.3.0` and `1.3.0` members, with `enableImmutableInstalls: true` in `.yarnrc.yml`: vendor, then the fresh install patched, then `vendor --revert` byte-exact, then re-vendor and `remove <purl>` byte-exact. A CRLF lock and package.json: vendor keeps CRLF and the revert is byte-exact.
- pass (not a bug): **hardened mode**. A lock with a `::__archiveUrl=` resolution passes `YARN_ENABLE_HARDENED_MODE=1 yarn install --immutable` and `--check-resolutions` on 4.12.0, with the registry reachable.
- observation, not filed: **zero-install** (`enableGlobalCache: false` with `.yarn/cache` committed). Hosted rewrites only `yarn.lock`, so the committed cache keeps the unpatched zip. `yarn install --immutable --immutable-cache`, yarn's recommended zero-install CI check, then fails YN0056 ("Cache entry required but missing"). A plain `--immutable` fetches the patched zip and swaps the cache files. This is a docs gap (hosted is documented as lock-only, and the zero-install cache isn't mentioned), not a defect.

### Ruled out
- `compressionLevel` from `YARN_COMPRESSION_LEVEL`, `~/.yarnrc.yml` or a parent rc: yarn bakes the level into the lock's `cacheKey` (`10c<level>`, `10` for mixed), and both modes already gate on `cacheKey`, so the project-rc-only read can't produce a wrong checksum. Low value; dropped from the backlog.

[agent] 2026-10-02: handover from the Yarn classic (1.x) bug-hunt routine (#304)

- **Reproduced on berry, so I commented on #519 instead of filing:** https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/519#issuecomment-5943684772. In a `nodeLinker: pnp` project installed from the registry lock, I pulled in a hosted `::__archiveUrl=` lock from a lock-only checkout. Before `yarn install`, `node -r ./.pnp.cjs` still loads the unpatched bytes, but standalone `vex` attests `not_affected` "(redirected)" with exit 0. This held on 4.0.2, 4.12.0 and 4.18.1 (2/2 runs each), and the attestation only becomes true after `yarn install --immutable`. Root cause is the same as #519 (`vex.rs:603-611`). On berry, though, lock-basis attestation under PnP is documented (yarn-berry-compatibility.md:11), so the fix needs a stale-install check rather than a blanket "PnP ⇒ not crawled".

### Cells (Linux)
- pass: vendored 4.12.0 with a `package.json` using tab indent, 4-space indent, a BOM, CRLF + tabs, no trailing newline, existing `resolutions` for another package, and an empty `resolutions` object. Every case got the fresh-checkout `--immutable --check-cache` patched bytes, the in-place immutable install, and a byte-exact `--revert` of package.json and yarn.lock. This is the #357 regression check.
- pass: vendored mixed CRLF/LF `yarn.lock` → `vendor_yarn_berry_mixed_line_endings` (loud, nothing written; yarn itself fails YN0028 there). A mixed `package.json` vendors and installs fine. Hosted mixed lock → `redirect_yarn_berry_mixed_line_endings`.
- pass: hosted 4.12.0 with the descriptors `npm:1.3.0`, `npm:^1.3.0`, devDependencies-only and optionalDependencies-only. Fresh `--immutable --check-cache` got patched bytes and left the lock unchanged.
- pass: hosted 4.12.0 and 4.18.1 for a legacy upper-case name (`JSONStream@1.3.5`, with registry deps) when the purl keeps its case.
- pass: agent apply / vex / rollback on yarn 2.4.2 (node-modules) and 3.8.7 (node-modules and pnpm linker, `.store/…/node_modules/left-pad` real dir). Rollback is byte-exact and idempotent, and vex reports `not_affected` after apply and exits 1 after rollback.

- Agent `apply` "applied: 2" for one purl came from my harness (a nested `fresh/` checkout under the project), not a crawler double-count.
- JSONStream fresh-install failure was my harness too: the poisoned `npmRegistryServer` blocks its registry deps.
- Rollback "Before blob not found" happened because my harness didn't stage the before-blob.

- If the patch API ever returns a lower-cased npm purl (`pkg:npm/jsonstream@1.3.5`, which the purl spec's npm rule suggests) for a legacy mixed-case package, every mode misses it: agent apply skips (exit 1), hosted gives `redirect_yarn_berry_entry_not_found`, vendored gives `vendor_lock_entry_not_found`. The crawler keeps the case (`pkg:npm/JSONStream@1.3.5`), and that end-to-end path passes. Whether the real API lower-cases is unknown from the sandbox, so I didn't file it. It's cross-PM (the npm crawler) if confirmed.

4. Hosted rollback/remove for `npm:` range and dev-only descriptors; vendored on the pnpm linker under v5.
